title: Generative AI editing: Generative Fill, Generative Expand, AI-assisted tools
author: echelon
body:
Forum feedback: "recent photoshop value proposition is AI and generative editing, did not see any of those features" and "Does it have generative fill?"

Deferred from the 0.2.0 release by decision: no generative backend has been chosen yet.

**Scope when picked up**
- Edit › Generative Fill (selection + prompt → new layer with masked result, several variations)
- Generative Expand (Crop tool beyond the canvas)
- Contextual task bar entry points (as in Photoshop)
- Backend chosen behind a provider interface (own Storyteller/ArtCraft API, or a third-party image model with user-supplied key); must stay off the wasm/offline path when unavailable
- Commands follow the usual rules: every action is an engine command, never panics, drivable over MCP

**Not covered here:** classical "smart" tools (Select Subject, Content-Aware Fill, Magic Eraser), which are handled without AI.

title: Image › Adjustments: Curves/Color Balance/Channel Mixer do nothing, no dialogs or live preview; adjustment Properties incomplete
author: echelon
body:
Forum feedback: *"The whole image adjustment section is very empty. Curves and many other panels do not work. And there is no preview when doing things."* Related: #13, #12.

**Verified defects**
- Image › Adjustments › **Curves, Color Balance, Channel Mixer** open no dialog and apply an identity no-op; **Black & White** and **Gradient Map** apply hard-coded defaults (`ui-egui/src/menus.rs` routes only kinds with slider tables; `engine/src/commands.rs` ignores their params).
- The slider dialogs (Levels, Hue/Sat, Brightness/Contrast, Exposure, Vibrance, Threshold, Posterize, Photo Filter) are generic slider lists with **no live preview**, no histogram, no per-channel or hue-range controls, and Photo Filter has no colour.
- Adjustment-layer Properties for **Color Balance, Black & White, Channel Mixer, Gradient Map** shows a placeholder ("arrive in milestone M7").

**Fix scope**
- Destructive Image › Adjustments dialogs reuse the adjustment-layer editors, with live canvas preview, OK commits one history step and Cancel restores.
- Full editors for every adjustment (Curves with channels and histogram, Levels with input/output levels and channels, Hue/Sat with ranges, Color Balance tones, B&W weights and tint, Channel Mixer, Gradient Map, Photo Filter colour), plus engine param parsing.
- Tests at 8/16/32-bit; snapshot-verified UI.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Curves: control points can't be deleted (no Delete key / Ctrl-click; pressing a point adds one)
author: echelon
body:
Forum feedback: *"control points in curves can't be deleted after being added"*

**Verified**: points are removed only by dragging more than 24px off the graph. There's no Delete/Backspace and no Ctrl/Cmd-click removal. The drag hit-test uses the pointer position after egui's drag threshold, so pressing on a point often **adds** a new one (`ui-egui/src/tone.rs`).

**Fix**: hit-test at the press origin; Delete/Backspace removes the selected point; Cmd/Ctrl-click deletes; a more forgiving drag-off; tests.

title: Ctrl + '+' scales the whole UI instead of zooming the canvas; Ctrl-modifier hotkey issues
author: echelon
body:
Forum feedback: *"I ended up enlarging the interface size when trying to zoom in using (Ctrl +)"* and *"improper hotkeys, ctrl-key hotkey modifiers"*.

**Verified**
- egui's keyboard UI zoom (`zoom_with_keyboard`) is left on. The app binds only Cmd/Ctrl+= and Cmd/Ctrl+-, so Ctrl+'+' (Shift+=, numpad +, '+' on Nordic/German layouts) falls through and scales the whole UI.
- View shortcuts are skipped while any dialog or text field has focus, so they also fall through to egui zoom.
- `snap_ui.rs` treats Ctrl as "disable snapping" on Windows/Linux, where Ctrl is the Command modifier.

**Fix**: disable egui keyboard zoom; bind Ctrl/Cmd + Plus/Equals/Minus/0 and numpad keys to view zoom; audit modifier handling; tests.

title: Elements can't be clicked while a dialog is open; clicking outside silently cancels the dialog
author: echelon
body:
Forum feedback: *"The interface is buggy; some elements can't be clicked"*.

**Verified**: every dialog is an `egui::Modal` with a transparent full-screen backdrop. Panels look live, but every click lands on the invisible backdrop, and the first such click silently **cancels** the dialog (`ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`). Photoshop lets you pan and zoom the canvas while an adjustment or filter dialog is open. Smaller items: the Studio-theme floating Properties card covers the canvas corner, the Magic Wand options are missing in Studio themes, and Delete/Backspace isn't bound to Edit › Clear.

**Fix**: tool dialogs don't close on outside click; canvas pan/zoom works with a dialog open; the other items; tests with egui_kittest.

title: Canvas isn't colour-managed: non-sRGB images (P3, Adobe RGB, ProPhoto, CMYK) display with wrong colours
author: echelon
body:
Forum feedback: *"the color is not right if you do not use an sRGB image"*.

**Verified**: embedded ICC profiles are read and kept, but the **canvas is not colour-managed**. The GPU canvas only applies a display LUT for Proof Colors / Gamut Warning / HDR preview; the CPU path applies none; the monitor profile is never set (assumed sRGB). Display P3 / Adobe RGB / ProPhoto images are shown with raw values (desaturated). Also: the embedded CMYK profile is ignored for display and flat export; EXR/HDR are treated as sRGB instead of linear; the 8-bit canvas texture clips 32-bit values.

**Fix**: always convert document profile → display (identity when equal) on both paths; read the monitor profile where the OS allows, else sRGB; use the embedded CMYK profile; tag EXR/HDR as linear; a 16F canvas texture for high-bit documents; tests with P3/AdobeRGB/ProPhoto/Gray/CMYK fixtures.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: macOS: double-clicking a PSD in Finder / Open With / Dock drop does nothing (PSD looks unsupported)
author: echelon
body:
Forum feedback: *"when will you add support for .PSD files?"*. PSD/PSB are fully supported, but on macOS **double-click in Finder, Open With and dropping on the Dock icon do nothing**: the app only reads paths from the command line, so the Info.plist document types have no effect. That's the most likely reason people think PSD is missing.

**Also verified**
- File › Open doesn't set the document path, so Cmd+S re-prompts and the name is the full path.
- Drag-and-drop onto the window doesn't set the path or Open Recent.
- Import/export warnings (e.g. 'adjustment flattened') are thrown away.
- `.pcraft` is missing from the Open and Save filters.

**Fix**: handle macOS open-documents events (no unsafe in our code); fix path/recent/warnings handling; tests.

title: PSD round trip: Vibrance, Color Balance, B&W, Photo Filter, Channel Mixer adjustment layers dropped on save
author: echelon
body:
Forum feedback: *"check whether layer blend modes and adjustment layers round trip correctly on export"*.

**Verified**: all 27 blend modes plus pass-through round-trip. But **Vibrance, Color Balance, Black & White, Photo Filter and Channel Mixer** adjustment layers are silently dropped when saving PSD (Photoshop sees an empty layer), and the same five blocks render as no-ops when importing a Photoshop file. The corpus test asserts no pass floor and never compares the exported file's composite.

**Fix**: read/write `vibA`, `blnc`, `blwh`, `phfl`, `mixr` from the Adobe spec; render them on import; a round-trip test for every adjustment kind and blend mode (export → reimport → composite equal); a corpus pass floor.

title: Large images (14k+): CPU fallback above 8192 px and ~6 GB peak memory; crashes on big files
author: echelon
body:
Forum feedback: *"opening and handling big images, 14k"*, *"it crashes with larger files"*, and a competitor's claim about performance.

**Verified for 14000×14000 (196 MP)**
- egui-wgpu requests `max_texture_dimension_2d = 8192`, so anything over 8192 px leaves the GPU compositor and every refresh uses the CPU path.
- `compose::render_tiled` holds two full-size f32 copies (~6.3 GB peak), and it runs per refresh, plus again for the navigator, channel thumbnails, histogram, export and save.
- Thumbnails flatten at full resolution.
- Export makes a per-pixel Vec.
- History has no memory cap.
- No benchmark covers more than 36 MP or 8192 px.

**Fix**: request the adapter's real limits; single-buffer `render_tiled`; proxy/downsampled thumbnails; banded export; history bounded by `memory_usage_mb`; a 14k/20k benchmark with peak-memory numbers recorded.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Camera RAW support: clean-room Rust decoder (DNG, CR2, NEF, ARW, …)
author: echelon
body:
Forum feedback: *"(Lossless) Compressed RAW support is a must"*, and a competitor's claim we have no raw support. Today TIFF-based raw files fail with a clear 'not supported' error (#25).

**Decision**: a clean-room, pure-Rust decoder (no LibRaw, no LGPL deps, no unsafe, wasm-safe), implemented from public specs.

**Scope (first cut)**
- DNG (uncompressed, lossless JPEG/LJ92, tiles, linearization, black/white levels, ColorMatrix/ForwardMatrix, AsShotNeutral)
- TIFF-based camera formats: CR2 (LJ92), NEF (lossless/compressed), ARW, PEF, ORF where feasible
- Demosaic (bilinear plus a higher-quality AHD/RCD-class option), white balance, camera → XYZ → working space, 16-bit output, embedded preview fallback
- Opens as a normal document; fuzzed and bounded against hostile input.

CR3 (ISO BMFF + CRX) and RAF/X-Trans are follow-ups.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Photoshop brush compatibility: .ABR import, stylus pressure/tilt, more presets
author: echelon
body:
Competitor claim: *"[no] brush engine with compatibility to photoshop brushes"*. The engine already models every Brush Settings section, but:
- there's **no .ABR import**
- pen **pressure/tilt are hard-coded to 1.0** on the canvas
- only ~5 built-in presets ship

**Fix**
- An .ABR importer (v1/v2 sampled tips and v6+ `samp` + `desc` dynamics mapped to our Brush settings), clean-room from public format descriptions
- Real stylus pressure/tilt where the platform delivers it
- A larger built-in preset set
- Optional: .GRD gradients and .ACO/.ASE swatches

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Plugin support: sandboxed WebAssembly plugin API (Filter › Plug-ins)
author: echelon
body:
Competitor claim: *"[no] support for photoshop plugins (including native)"*.

**Decision**: hosting native .8BF binaries would require unsafe FFI and can't work on web, so PhotoCraft gets a **sandboxed WebAssembly plugin API** instead: plugins are .wasm modules run by a pure-Rust runtime with resource limits, which can read and write pixels of the active layer/selection and register filters under Filter › Plug-ins. No filesystem or network access by default. The Plug-ins preference folder is honoured.

Includes an example plugin, docs and tests (including hostile modules: infinite loops, memory bombs).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Magic Eraser and Background Eraser tools; Magic Wand options missing in Studio themes

Forum feedback: *"how good is the magic wand tool and Magic eraser?"*. Magic Wand works (tolerance, contiguous, anti-alias, sample all layers), but **Magic Eraser and Background Eraser don't exist**, and the Magic Wand options bar is missing in Studio themes.

title: Stylus pressure/tilt on macOS and Linux
author: echelon
body:
Follow-up to #74. Real pen pressure reaches the brush engine on Windows (winit Force via egui-winit) and on the web (Pointer Events: pressure, tilt and twist). On macOS and Linux, winit 0.30 / egui-winit 0.36 deliver no pressure, so strokes use 1.0. Details are in `crates/ui-egui/src/stylus.rs`. Options: a winit upgrade that exposes tablet events, or a maintained safe crate for NSEvent pressure / XInput2 valuators (this workspace forbids unsafe code).

title: Useful PSD compatibility test corpus from psd-tools
author: egofree71
body:
Hi, I thought this might be useful for PhotoCraft as the PSD support matures.
The psd-tools project includes a large collection of PSD test files covering many edge cases:
https://github.com/psd-tools/psd-tools/tree/main/tests/psd_files
I’ve been using some of these files to compare Photoshop-compatible editors against Photoshop, and they’re very useful for finding subtle rendering and compatibility issues involving blending, clipping, layer effects, masks, patterns, text, color modes, higher bit depths, and other PSD features.
I know PhotoCraft is still at an early stage and doesn’t support all of these cases yet, but this could still be a useful corpus for future compatibility and regression testing.
Just sharing it as a useful resource — feel free to close the issue if you prefer to track this elsewhere.

title: Gaussian Blur dialog shows two competing sliders with different sensitivities
author: migero
body:
## Problem

The **Gaussian Blur** filter dialog (Effects → Blur → Gaussian Blur) displays two sliders that control the same "Radius" parameter:
- One regular (linear) slider
- One logarithmic slider

These sliders have very different sensitivities, making it confusing and difficult to adjust the blur radius precisely. One slider will be sensitive at low values while the other is sensitive at high values.

## Root Cause

In `crates/ui-egui/src/filter_dialog.rs` (lines 271-283), when a parameter has a huge range (max/min ratio > 500), the code creates both:
1. A `slider_row()` on line 275 - intended as a numeric input field but renders as a full slider
2. A logarithmic `slider()` on line 277 - for better control across the range

Both are rendered and both modify the same value, creating competing controls.

### Code Location:
**File:** `crates/ui-egui/src/filter_dialog.rs:271-283`

```rust
let logarithmic = min > 0.0 && max / min > 500.0;
if logarithmic {
    // Scrub the value field directly; add a log-scaled slider for huge ranges.
    let mut lv = v.max(min.max(0.1)).ln();
    let r = crate::widgets::slider_row(ui, &label(&p.key), &mut v, min..=max, unit, None);  // ← Problem: Creates visible slider
    let _ = r;
    let r2 = crate::widgets::slider(ui, &mut lv, min.max(0.1).ln()..=max.ln(), None);        // ← Also creates slider
    if r2.changed() {
        v = lv.exp();
    }
}
```

## Solution

The intent was to have:
- A **numeric input field** for direct value entry (not a slider)
- A **logarithmic slider** for intuitive dragging control across the huge range

Options:
1. Hide the `slider_row()` output or replace it with a numeric text field only
2. Use only the logarithmic slider with a separate numeric input
3. Make the first slider logarithmic too for consistency

The Gaussian Blur's radius range (0.1 to 1000 pixels) is one of the few parameters with such an extreme ratio, making this UI issue visible to users.

title: Publish apps on Flathub
author: deadmeu
body:
With working Flatpaks and bundles being introduced as Release artifacts soon with #163 (and hopefully all the other apps too) it would be great if they were also published on Flathub directly, which is the primary distribution platform for Flatpaks.

This would make it as simple as possible for new users to install and use the software, which has historically been a major pain-point for these sorts of creative applications. Professional-grade software, such as DaVinci Resolve, has famously been very difficult to install and run on Linux, outside of its very narrow supported installation methods. Making the ArtCraft apps available on Flathub would platform them above the alternatives. This first-class support for Flatpaks on Linux would also help those running immutable distributions (such as Valve's Steam Deck and Fedora's Atomic distributions) to more easily install and use the software.

Submission documentation is available at https://docs.flathub.org/docs/for-app-authors/submission and there are many Flatpaks already submitted to be used as templates. Please ensure you fully understand https://docs.flathub.org/docs/for-app-authors/requirements before submitting, as there may be some issues with the current standing of these apps (especially given they are entirely AI written). Take particular care around https://docs.flathub.org/docs/for-app-authors/requirements#insufficient-development-history (this may require a significant delay of at least a few months until Flathub is available to you as a distribution platform), and especially https://docs.flathub.org/docs/for-app-authors/requirements#generative-ai-policy which notes "Flathub manifests must not contain AI-generated or AI-assisted content. Disclosure does not exempt manifests from this restriction".

title: Brush stroke preview draws a hard black polygon while painting, then snaps to the real stroke on release
author: echelon
body:
User report from Reddit: https://www.reddit.com/r/OpenAI/comments/1wxmunv/comment/pdz1tep/?screen_view_count=3

Recording: https://i.redd.it/zn9eknm2ylth1.gif (viewer: https://www.reddit.com/media?url=https%3A%2F%2Fi.redd.it%2Fzn9eknm2ylth1.gif)

## What happens (from the recording)

Brush tool, soft round brush, black foreground, dark blue canvas (zoomed in, pixel grid visible).

1. **While the mouse button is down**, the live stroke preview isn't drawn as a soft brush. It shows a **hard-edged, solid black polygon** that fans out from the stroke's start point. It looks like pie wedges or a triangle fan joining the start point to each new cursor position, plus round-ish caps. The shape grows into a large blob covering an area the brush never touched, and it also covers the existing white stroke.
2. **On mouse release** it snaps to the correct result: a soft-edged black stroke along the actual path.

So the committed stroke is right, but the in-progress preview is badly wrong, which reads as heavy flicker or "drawing a different shape" while painting.

## Suspects

- The live-stroke preview path (#64 LiveStroke, #86 smoothing tail): the in-progress dabs/outline appear to be filled as one polygon (non-zero/fan fill from the first vertex) instead of being stamped as dabs.
- Canvas refresh during strokes (#71, #84): the preview overlay vs the committed tiles.

## Expected

The preview while dragging matches the committed stroke (soft dabs along the path), like Photoshop, with no visual change on release.

## To do

- Reproduce with a soft round brush at high zoom (and at 100%), on CPU and GPU canvas paths.
- Add a test that the live preview raster equals the committed stroke raster for the same input points.

title: CR2: hard-coded RGGB colour pattern gives a magenta cast on several Canon models (7D, 40D, 550D, 5D Mark II)
author: niklasrichardson
body:
## Problem

`crates/raw/src/cr2.rs:166-167` uses one colour filter (CFA) pattern for every Canon CR2:

```rust
// Canon sensors are RGGB from the top-left of the image area.
let cfa = Cfa { width: 2, height: 2, colors: vec![0, 1, 1, 2], origin_x: active.x, origin_y: active.y };
```

That assumption does not hold for every Canon model. On the affected models, green sites are read as red/blue and the other way round, so every photo from those cameras has a magenta cast.

CR2 files have no `CFAPattern` tag, so the pattern probably needs to come from a per-model table.

Related: #50 (camera raw support). LightCraft has the same bug in its own decoder: storytold/lightcraft#85.

1. Download a 7D sample (CC0): https://raw.pixls.us/data/Canon/EOS%207D/RAW_CANON_EOS_7D-raw.CR2
2. Run `photocraft-cli convert RAW_CANON_EOS_7D-raw.CR2 out.jpg`
3. **Expected:** natural colours. **Actual:** the whole image has a magenta cast.

PhotoCraft `main` at `ff53be7`, Windows 11, `photocraft-cli convert`, one CC0 sample per model from raw.pixls.us.

title: HOSTING.md says the wasm is "about 13 MB", but v0.2.0 ships 25.8 MiB (breaks Cloudflare 25 MiB asset limit)
author: htdtkshi
body:
`HOSTING.md` in `photocraft-web-0.2.0.zip` says:

> `photocraft-web-<hash>_bg.wasm` — The app, about 13 MB, or 5 MB with compression

and lists Cloudflare Pages as a target for the sample `_headers`.

In the v0.2.0 zip (SHA256 matches SHA256SUMS.txt) the file is 27,072,762 bytes (25.8 MiB). Running `wasm-opt -Oz` (binaryen v108 and v132) only gets it to ~26.2 MB, still just over 26,214,400 bytes (25 MiB), which is the per-file limit for Cloudflare Workers static assets / Pages. A plain upload therefore fails.

Brotli gives 6,773,693 bytes (gzip 10,714,100), so the "5 MB with compression" figure is also optimistic.

Workaround that worked in local `wrangler dev` + headless Chromium: upload `*_bg.wasm.br` as an asset and have a small Worker return it with `Content-Type: application/wasm` and `Content-Encoding: br`, using `new Response(body, { encodeBody: "manual", ... })` (without `encodeBody: "manual"` the browser receives undecoded brotli and fails with `expected magic word 00 61 73 6d`). The SRI hash in index.html stays valid because it is over the decoded bytes.

Suggestion: correct the size in HOSTING.md, and either document the limit plus this workaround or shrink the binary.

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04, Chromium via Playwright, v0.2.0.

title: Saving is not atomic: a failed or interrupted save can destroy the user's file
author: echelon
body:
Saving a document writes the destination file in place: `apps/photocraft/src/services.rs:125` (`std::fs::write(path, bytes)`), `crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs:91` and `crates/automation/src/files.rs`. A crash, full disk or killed process mid-write leaves a truncated PSD and the user's previous good file is gone. Only prefs, presets and `.pcraft` bundles use temp-file + rename, and none of them fsync.

## Fix
One shared `atomic_write(path, bytes)` used by every document write (Save, Save As, Export, Save for Web, batch, automation):
- write to a temp file in the **same directory**, `sync_all()`, rename over the target, fsync the directory (Unix)
- Windows: retry the rename with backoff on `PermissionDenied` (EPERM / sharing violation from antivirus or indexers); fall back to `ReplaceFileW`-style replace semantics via std
- cross-device (`EXDEV`, e.g. temp dir on another volume): never happens if the temp file sits beside the target; if the directory isn't writable, error clearly instead of writing in place
- on any failure, the original file is untouched and the temp file is removed

## Tests
Failure injection through the platform-services seam: write error halfway, rename error, read-only directory. Assert the original bytes survive in every case. Never-crash rules apply.

title: Preferences that do nothing, and recent files lost on restart
author: echelon
body:
Several settings appear in Preferences but nothing reads them: `interface.ui_scale`, `ui_font_size`, `show_channels_in_color`, `dynamic_color_sliders`, `show_tooltips`, `workspace.large_tabs`, `general.animated_zoom`, `auto_show_home_screen` (all in `crates/engine/src/prefs.rs`). The RAW prefs (colour space, auto tone, open as Smart Object) and `ask_before_saving_layered_tiff` are also never read. Changing them has no effect, which users will see as broken.

On top of that, **recent files are lost on restart**: `app.ui.recent_files` is never written to `prefs.file_handling.recent_files`, and `recent_file_count` (default 20) is ignored (the list is capped at 10).

## Fix
- Wire up each preference, or hide it until it works. A dialog control that does nothing is worse than a missing one.
- Persist recent files through prefs and honour `recent_file_count`.
- Add a test that walks every `Prefs` field and asserts it is either read somewhere or listed in an explicit "not yet implemented, hidden" allowlist, so this can't regress.

title: Free Transform with a selection misaligns a linked layer mask
author: echelon
body:
`crates/engine/src/transform_cmds.rs` (`transform_layer`, ~lines 111–131): when a selection is active, Free Transform moves only the selected pixels (`split_selected`), but a **linked layer mask is warped as a whole**. Afterwards the mask no longer lines up with the pixels.

Related gaps found at the same time:
- the live transform preview (`crates/ui-egui/src/transform_tool.rs` `preview_image`) draws the layer without its mask applied
- `edit.transform` ignores `"target":"mask"`, so a targeted, unlinked mask can't be transformed by itself (Photoshop transforms just the mask)

## Tests
- linked raster mask + no selection: mask moves with the pixels (exists for vector masks; add one for raster masks)
- linked raster mask + selection: only the selected region of the mask moves, and pixels and mask stay aligned
- unlinked mask: stays put
- targeted mask: only the mask transforms

title: PSD text loses manual and optical kerning on import and export
author: echelon
body:
`crates/text/src/psd.rs` (~lines 264 and 380): on import, Optical kerning is mapped to Metrics and manual per-pair `Kerning` values are dropped. On export, every run is written with `"Kerning": 0`. Opening and re-saving a professionally kerned PSD silently changes its typography. This is data loss.

## Fix
1. Model manual kerning per character (1/1000 em, the value stored in the PSD) in `CharStyle`, and keep the Auto-kern mode (Metrics / Optical / Off) separately.
2. Read and write both exactly. Until optical kerning is rendered, keep the Optical flag rather than downgrading it, so it round-trips.
3. Then implement the UI: Alt+←/→ with a collapsed caret adjusts the pair (Photoshop behaviour), plus the Character panel field.

## Tests
A PSD round trip of a run with manual kerning and one with Optical kerning, byte-equal on the kerning fields. Add a real Photoshop-authored file to the oracle corpus.

title: Retouch tools ignore the mask/channel target; Sample All Layers ignored by Blur/Sharpen/Smudge
author: echelon
body:
Retouch tools write to the layer's pixels even when a layer mask, an alpha channel or Quick Mask is targeted: `run_stroke` in `crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds.rs` (~line 83) never consults the paint target. This affects Clone Stamp, Healing, Spot Healing, Smudge, Blur, Sharpen, Dodge, Burn, Sponge and History Brush. Brush, Eraser, Gradient and Paint Bucket already route through `paint_target()`.

Related:
- **Sample All Layers is ignored for Blur, Sharpen and Smudge.** The checkbox exists (`crates/ui-egui/src/retouch_ui.rs`) but `finish_stroke` never passes it to the command.
- **Smudge mixes straight (non-premultiplied) RGBA** (`crates/paint/src/retouch.rs`), so colour from transparent pixels bleeds in and leaves dark fringes around soft edges.
- `edit.transform` also ignores alpha-channel targets.

## Tests
For each retouch tool: a stroke with a mask targeted changes only the mask; with an alpha channel targeted, only the channel. Sample All Layers changes the result over a two-layer document. Smudging across a transparent edge leaves no dark fringe (premultiplied mixing).

title: Marquee: Shift doesn't constrain to a square (always passed false); no Alt-from-centre or size readout
author: echelon
body:
Shift while dragging a Rectangular or Elliptical Marquee should constrain to a square or circle. In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, both the preview (~line 1498) and the commit (~line 1769) call `chrome_ui::marquee_end(..., false, ...)` with `shift` hard-coded to `false`, even though `marquee_end` implements and tests the constraint.

Also missing while dragging a marquee:
- **Alt draws from the centre** (not implemented)
- a **W × H px readout** beside the cursor
- the add/subtract/intersect intent must keep working when the modifier was pressed before the drag (it does since #188; keep a test so it stays that way)

## Tests
A kittest dragging with Shift held commits a square selection; with Alt, a selection centred on the press point; and the readout text matches the selection size.

title: Performance: interactive edits on layered documents redraw only what changed
author: echelon
body:
Generic edits redraw the whole document. `Session::edit` sets `last_damage = None` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs` ~373), and undo and redo do the same, so moving a layer, changing opacity, blend mode or visibility, and every undo recomposite everything. Only brush, eraser, retouch and type commands report a damage rect. Work on the `perf/layout-documents` branch (#125/#128) fixes move and setProps; this issue tracks the rest and the measured targets.

## Targets (release build, layered 20 MP PSD with styled layers; p95 unless noted)
| Interaction | Target |
|---|---|
| Move a layer with layer styles (per update while dragging) | ≤ 25 ms |
| Change layer opacity / fill / blend mode | ≤ 20 ms |
| Toggle visibility | ≤ 10 ms |
| Undo / redo of a move or property change | ≤ 25 ms |
| Paste or duplicate a 12 MP layer (first / repeat) | ≤ 100 ms / ≤ 20 ms |
| Arrow-key nudge in a 150-layer document | ≤ 30 ms |
| Edits on a 15000×10000 16-bit document | ≤ 80 ms |
| Zoom / pan frame time on the same | ≤ 16 ms |
| 32-bit float document with 20 layers: any edit | ≤ 100 ms |

## Work
- Damage rects for `layer.translate`, `layer.setProps`, paste, duplicate, and undo/redo (store the damage with each history step).
- `History::trim` hashes every tile of every state on each edit (`crates/ops/src/lib.rs` ~125): make it incremental.
- Layout documents: per-layer chunk culling in the GPU planner (#128).
- Benchmark rows for each target in the perf scorecard (see the scorecard issue).

title: Performance: background jobs with progress and cancel for long operations
author: echelon
body:
Every long operation runs synchronously on the UI thread, and none can be cancelled: opening files (`file_open.rs` reads and decodes everything up front), filters, Content-Aware Fill and Scale, Photomerge, ABR import, batch processing, and the commits of Warp, Puppet Warp, Perspective Warp and Liquify. A slow operation freezes the window, and the user can't stop it.

## Goal
A small engine job system: run a command on a worker, show progress, cancel, and apply the result as one undo step. The UI stays at 60 fps throughout. Native uses threads; wasm runs inline (or a worker later), with the same API.

## Targets
| Operation | Target |
|---|---|
| Open a 20 MP layered PSD | first pixels ≤ 1 s, editable ≤ 3 s, UI never blocked |
| Open a 2 GB PSD / 4–5 GB PSB | opens with progress, editable, never blank |
| Content-Aware Fill on 10 MP | ≤ 1.5 s, cancellable |
| Spot Healing / Healing on 10 MP | ≤ 0.5 s per stroke |
| Warp / Puppet / Perspective preview at 4K | ≤ 16 ms per frame, commit in the background |
| Import 500 brushes | no UI pause over 100 ms |
| Any job | cancel takes effect within 200 ms and leaves the document unchanged |

## Work
- `Job` API in the engine: progress callback, `CancelToken`, result applied on the UI thread; panics caught (never-crash).
- Move open, import, filters, retouch fills, warps, batch and ABR import onto it.
- Progress plus Cancel UI (status bar and a modal for blocking ops), Esc cancels.
- Streaming or banded PSD decode so layers become visible before the whole file is decoded.

title: Performance: fix slow algorithms (feather/smooth, Content-Aware Scale, Select Subject, Liquify, brush release)
author: echelon
body:
Several algorithms are far slower than they should be at real image sizes.

| Operation | Problem | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Select › Modify › Smooth / Feather on 24 MP | `algo/src/selection.rs` uses a naive O(N·r) box blur and a direct O(N·6σ) Gaussian, single-threaded: many seconds at large radii | ≤ 100 ms (running-sum box / recursive Gaussian, which `algo` already has for Blur, plus rayon) |
| Content-Aware Scale 24 MP | `algo/src/seam.rs` recomputes the full energy map and DP per seam, single-threaded: minutes | ≤ 3 s; interactive proxy preview while dragging |
| Select Subject / Object Selection, repeated | superpixels, GMMs and pyramid recomputed on every call | ≤ 100 ms for repeat runs (cache per layer revision) |
| Liquify 800 px brush on 3500×2200 | proxy capped at 1600 px, so not full resolution | ≤ 1 ms per update at full resolution when zoomed in |
| Camera Raw exposure change (proxy) | synchronous 900 px CPU proxy, never timed | ≤ 10 ms |
| Brush release on long strokes | mouse-up re-renders the whole stroke | reuse the live renderer's result; no hitch at release |
| Brush on A4 300 dpi CMYK | not measured | ≤ 6 ms dab-to-screen |
| Brush preview memory, small dab on an 8K viewport | not measured | ≤ 2 MiB |
| Marquee drag on 24 MP with Alt/Shift | not measured | ≤ 17 ms p95 |

Each fix comes with a benchmark row in the scorecard and a before/after entry in the dev log. Wasm must keep building (use the `par_*` helpers).

title: Reliability: recover from out-of-memory during paste, erase, fill and save; auto-PSB above 2 GB
author: echelon
body:
Never-crash covers panics, but a Rust allocation failure aborts the process, and the panic guard can't catch it. Paste, erase, fill and save allocate full-size buffers infallibly. Only flat export uses `try_reserve`.

## Work
- Fallible allocation (`try_reserve` / checked sizes) for surface and region allocations reachable from paste, erase, fill, transform, save and import. Return a clear "not enough memory for this operation" error and keep the document intact.
- Export: switch to PSB automatically when the estimated file size exceeds 2 GB, not only when a side exceeds 30000 px (`psd_export.rs`). A >2 GB `.psd` can't be opened by Photoshop.
- Tests: an allocation-limit injection (cap via the existing `max_alloc` options or a test hook) makes each of those commands return `Err` with the document unchanged.

title: Tools: painting and retouching gaps (Pencil, Mixer, Patch, Content-Aware Move, Fill dialog, live previews)
author: echelon
body:
Gaps in the painting and retouching tools, measured against Photoshop's behaviour. Each item is done when it has a command, a UI, and tests.

## Missing tools
- [ ] **Pencil** tool (`paint.pencil` exists in the engine, but there's no tool): aliased 1 px painting, a square cursor aligned to the pixel grid
- [ ] **Mixer Brush** tool (`paint.mixerBrush` exists in the engine, but there's no tool)
- [ ] **Patch** tool, with a live preview of the patched area
- [ ] **Content-Aware Move** tool (reuse `inpaint::complete`)

## Behaviour
- [ ] Painting on a type, shape, Smart Object or fill layer asks "Rasterize this layer?" and continues the stroke, instead of failing silently in the status bar
- [ ] **Edit › Fill… dialog**: contents (Foreground/Background/Color/Pattern/History/Content-Aware), blend mode, opacity, preserve transparency. It remembers the last choices across restarts. Shift+Backspace opens it.
- [ ] **Live stroke preview for every brush-based tool** (Clone, Heal, Smudge, Blur, Sharpen, Dodge, Burn, Sponge, History Brush). Today only Brush and Eraser preview live; the others draw a translucent trail and apply on release.
- [ ] Clone Source: a W/H link toggle; draw the clone overlay (opacity, blend, clipped, auto-hide); Alt shows a target cursor
- [ ] Eyedropper comparison ring while sampling (new colour above, current colour below)
- [ ] Brush size and hardness drag (Ctrl+Alt on Windows, Ctrl+Opt on Mac) with an on-canvas size readout
- [ ] Editable pressure curve (global, and per control)
- [ ] Import an image file as a brush tip
- [ ] Regression tests: pressure→opacity strokes show no tile seams or square artifacts; hard round edge profile; default presets have zero scatter; ABR textures (RGB, indexed, CMYK, missing pattern) never decode to black
- [ ] Tablet: verify that no OS arrow cursor appears over the canvas (macOS, Windows, Linux)

Also see #207 (retouch target and Sample All Layers bugs).

title: Tools: selection, transform and drawing gaps (Select and Mask, Move marquee, transform menu, Pen, Crop, Vanishing Point)
author: echelon
body:
Gaps in the selection, transform and drawing tools. Each item is done when it has a command, a UI, and tests.

## Selection
- [ ] **Select and Mask workspace**: ≥5 view modes (Onion Skin, Marching Ants, Overlay, On Black, On White, B&W, On Layers), Refine Edge brush, all 6 outputs (adds New Document). Today it's a generic parameter dialog with no view modes and 4 outputs.
- [ ] Marquee: Shift square, Alt from centre, live W × H readout (#208)
- [ ] Color Range: an explicit test for Sampled Colors at Fuzziness 0 (exact match)

## Move and transform
- [ ] Move tool: drag a box on empty canvas to select every layer it touches; hover outlines with Auto-Select; double-click fits the image; drag layers onto another document's tab to copy them there
- [ ] Canvas right-click menu during Free Transform (Scale, Rotate, Skew, Distort, Perspective, Warp, Flip, Rotate 90/180)
- [ ] Puppet Warp mesh follows the object's outline (constrained triangulation of the traced alpha) instead of a block grid, so gaps stay open and separate pieces move independently
- [ ] Content-Aware Scale driven by the Free Transform box with a live proxy preview
- [ ] Ruler tool: a measured angle prefills Image › Image Rotation › Arbitrary (to 0.01°)
- [ ] Crop: W × H × Resolution with units (px, in, cm, mm, pt, pica, %), saved crop presets, Straighten in the options bar

## Pen and shapes
- [ ] Pen: Alt breaks a handle, Shift snaps to 45°, Ctrl temporarily Direct Selects, Backspace removes the last anchor, drag a handle when closing a path
- [ ] Stroke Path dialog: choose among the brush-based tools, plus Simulate Pressure
- [ ] Shapes: rounded-rectangle corner handles on the canvas (all corners; Alt for one corner); shape feather; one-step Selection → editable Shape with a simplify tolerance
- [ ] Mask Properties: Density and Feather controls (feather rendering landed in #195)

## Filters with on-canvas UI
- [ ] Vanishing Point: an interactive window to draw and edit planes, paste, and clone in perspe…

title: File compatibility: Smart Objects/Filters in PSD, layered TIFF, SVG, PDF, RAW, swatches, contours, advanced blending
author: echelon
body:
Document and file-format gaps, measured against what Photoshop reads and writes. The PSD core is in good shape (see the corpus floors). These are the remaining holes, roughly in priority order.

## Smart Objects and Smart Filters (highest impact)
- [ ] **Export Smart Objects as Smart Objects.** Any edit, and any Smart Object created in PhotoCraft, is written to PSD as flat pixels (`psd_export.rs`, `detach_psd()`). Write `SoLd` + `lnk2` with the embedded document (`encode_linked_file` exists but is only used in tests).
- [ ] **Smart Filters survive PSD save and open.** Import drops them (`psd_import.rs` sets `smart_filters` to empty); export rasterizes. Parse and write the `filterFX` descriptor.
- [ ] Filter-mask painting with undo (today the mask comes only from the selection when the filter is applied)
- [ ] Adjustments as Smart Filters (Hue/Saturation with Colorize and ranges, Curves, Levels, Shadows/Highlights)
- [ ] Smart Filter rows: collapse triangle, real mask thumbnail, blending-options icon, drag to reorder, right-click menu, live preview while re-editing
- [ ] Smart Object corner skew and perspective (store a quad or homography instead of an affine)

## Formats
- [ ] **Layered TIFF**: read and write Photoshop layer data (tag 37724) using the PSD layer writer; honour `ask_before_saving_layered_tiff`
- [ ] Large and BigTIFF import (banded decode), all IFDs
- [ ] **SVG**: open and place as shape layers or a vector Smart Object
- [ ] **PDF**: multi-page Save As PDF, PDF Presentation, Layer Comps to PDF; vector and text output; PDF import
- [ ] RAW: lossy-JPEG DNG (Samsung Expert RAW and others), highlight reconstruction modes, `.xmp` sidecar read and write, wire up the RAW prefs; a raw.pixls.us corpus with per-camera coverage numbers
- [ ] Camera Raw dialog: histogram; settings persist as a PSD Smart Filter
- [ ] Video and footage layers: persist frames in `.pcraft`; map PSD video layers
- [ ] Swatches: a user swatch model plus ACO/ASE import and export (the p…

title: File compatibility measurement: corpora in CI, large-file, TIFF/RAW/EXR corpora, Photoshop re-open check
author: echelon
body:
How we measure file compatibility has gaps. The PSD corpora are good, but they don't cover everything we claim.

- [ ] **Run every corpus in CI.** Fetch corpora in CI with a cache keyed by the pin. In progress in #190 (`cargo xtask corpus --all`, https://github.com/storytold/photocraft-corpus). Until then the PASS/ROUNDTRIP floors only hold on machines that have the files.
- [ ] **Large real-world files:** a pinned 20 MP layered PSD, a 150-layer layout PSD, and generated 2 GB PSD and 4–5 GB PSB stress files (generated at test time, not stored). Used by both the fidelity tests and the perf scorecard.
- [ ] **TIFF, RAW and EXR corpora with tests.** `xtask corpus` lists `corpus/tiff`, `corpus/raw` and `corpus/exr`, but no test reads them. Report per-camera RAW coverage as a number.
- [ ] **Photoshop opens what we export.** Today's round trip is our export → our import. Add a Photoshop-side check: the oracle generator re-opens our exports in Photoshop and saves its composite, and we compare. The script approach already exists from the Photoshop oracle work.
- [ ] **Save-path tests with no coverage today:** layered TIFF, PDF, SVG, ACO/ASE, `.shc`, Smart Filter persistence, atomic-save failure injection.
- [ ] **Workflow acceptance tests** (roadmap "Making it measurable", item 1): 30–50 end-to-end tasks driven through MCP or commands.

title: Workspace and UI: persistence, floating panels, tabs, palette, numeric fields, Layers/Curves/Color panels
author: echelon
body:
Workspace and UI gaps. Each item is done when it works, persists where relevant, and has a kittest.

## Persistence (users notice these first)
- [ ] Tool options, the last Export As and Save for Web settings, Fill settings, brush subtools, and font recents/favourites survive restarts (`ToolOptions` isn't persisted today; Export always opens at png/85)
- [ ] Window size and dock width are remembered (no eframe persistence today; the dock snapshot omits the width)
- [ ] File › Open starts in the last-used folder
- [ ] Also #204 (preferences that do nothing, recent files lost)

## Workspace
- [ ] Panels can float: "Float in Window" and dragging a group's title out of the dock; floating groups restored at launch
- [ ] Document tabs: overflow menu listing all open documents, right-click menu (Close, Close Others, Close All, Reveal), drag to reorder
- [ ] Command palette (Cmd+K): an empty query shows recently run commands
- [ ] Canvas right-click menu (tool-specific, like Photoshop); right-click spelling suggestions in type and text fields
- [ ] UI scale presets 100 / 115 / 125 / 150 / 200 % applied through egui `zoom_factor` and remembered
- [ ] Appearance: toggle UI animation; toggle the canvas background pattern for every theme; show recent files on the start screen, with an option to hide them
- [ ] Themes: add a soft dark and a soft light theme, with previews in the theme picker; outline slider knobs in light themes (contrast check). Update `docs/ui-design.md` (it lists the wrong default and count).
- [ ] Document presets: save custom New Document presets; a real "Recent" category

## Controls
- [ ] Numeric fields accept arithmetic (`90+45`, `1920/2`, unit suffixes); labels scrub when dragged; double-click a slider to reset it to its default
- [ ] Layers panel: scroll the wheel over the blend-mode dropdown to step through modes; drop a layer on the New Layer button to duplicate it and on Trash to delete it; checkerboard drawn only behind the artwork
- [ ] Curves: smo…

title: Type: type on a path, RTL/complex scripts, variable fonts, OpenType UI, kerning, Warp Text preview
author: echelon
body:
Type gaps. The shaping core (parley/HarfRust, bidi) is solid; most gaps are in the model and UI.

- [ ] **Type on a path**: a `TextShape::Path` variant (path, start/end offsets, flip); glyphs laid out along the arc length; clicking a path with the Type tool starts path text; the caret and selection follow the curve; PSD path text imported and exported (today `TySh` path text is kept as raw data only)
- [ ] **Paragraph direction** control (Auto/LTR/RTL) in the Paragraph panel and options bar (the engine supports it; there's no UI); visual caret movement in RTL text
- [ ] **Script coverage**: Thai, Khmer and Indic (Devanagari etc.) fonts in the fallback chain; consider bundling Noto subsets for the web build. Golden shaping tests for Arabic joining and marks, Hebrew, Devanagari conjuncts, Thai, Khmer, and LTR numerals inside RTL text.
- [ ] **Variable fonts**: sliders for each axis from `FaceInfo.axes`; `opsz` follows the point size automatically
- [ ] **OpenType UI**: Character panel buttons, and Numerals (lining, oldstyle, tabular, proportional) and Stylistic Sets (ss01–ss20) submenus (the features already render)
- [ ] **Kerning**: manual pair kerning with Alt+←/→, optical kerning rendered, and both round-tripped through PSD (#206)
- [ ] **Warp Text** dialog previews live and opens with the layer's current warp (today it always starts at Arc)
- [ ] Editing tests: Cmd+A selects all text while editing; double-click selects a word, triple-click a line, quadruple-click a paragraph; paste
- [ ] Optional: offer "Rasterize and continue?" for Distort, Perspective and Warp on live type instead of a bare error

title: Automation: Actions that replay reliably, Batch options, plug-in panels, local ML models, agent coverage
author: echelon
body:
Automation and extensibility gaps.

## Actions
- [ ] Record steps in a document-independent form: drop the explicit `layer` id when it was the active layer, and collapse a run of type keystrokes into one create/edit step. Today, styled-text and layer-targeted steps replay against the wrong layer in another document.
- [ ] Per-step enable checkboxes, dialog toggles, reorder, delete single steps, Insert Stop, action sets, `.atn` import
- [ ] `actions.record/stop/play/list` commands, so agents and the CLI can drive Actions
- [ ] Replay tests for crop, filters, selections and styled text on a second document

## Batch
- [ ] Include subfolders (mirroring the folder tree in the output), "open documents" as a source, a naming template (`{name}{serial}{date}`), per-format options, progress and cancel (needs #210), an error-log file, stop-on-error

## Plug-ins and local models
- [ ] Plug-in ABI v2: a `panel` kind (declarative UI rendered by the app), progress and cancel host calls, reading other layers, Last Filter repeats plug-ins
- [ ] Local ML models (ONNX) behind a feature flag: load, reload and manage models in Preferences; first users are Select Subject / Object Selection and Remove Background. Storage must work in AppImage and Flatpak.
- Generative AI stays tracked in #41 (deferred by decision).

## Agent coverage
- [ ] An `xtask` check that every panel button routes through a command id
- [ ] Headless commands for things only reachable through pointer and key events today: in-canvas type editing, Liquify/Puppet strokes, transform handles
- [ ] Grow the M11 agent acceptance suite toward 30–50 workflows

title: Distribution: update checks, Windows ARM64, in-app bug report, localisation coverage
author: echelon
body:
Distribution and feedback gaps.

- [ ] **Update check**: Help › Check for Updates, plus an opt-out periodic check against GitHub Releases on macOS, Windows and Linux, showing what's new and a download link. No auto-install yet. No personal data is sent; it only fetches the public releases feed.
- [ ] **Windows ARM64** build (`aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`) in the release matrix, signed like x64
- [ ] **In-app bug report**: a dialog that gathers the version, OS, GPU adapter, document stats (no pixels), an optional screenshot and the recent log. The user reviews it and it opens a prefilled GitHub issue (the user must be able to see everything that will be sent). Up to three optional attachments.
- [ ] **Localisation** coverage measured: `xtask` reports the share of UI strings translated per language once #169 (i18n foundation) lands; RTL UI layout for Arabic and Hebrew
- [ ] Linux: AppImage x86_64 and aarch64 already ship; keep Flatpak (#163); Flathub later (#173), as already agreed

title: Scorecard: measure performance, tools, compatibility and features with numbers CI keeps current
author: echelon
body:
We need one place that says, with numbers, how PhotoCraft is doing in every area that matters to people choosing an image editor: **performance, tools, file compatibility, features, workspace, type, automation and reliability**. "Parity" in `docs/parity.md` only measures menu wiring, and the honest assessment in the roadmap is a judgment call. The scorecard turns both into measurements that CI keeps current.

## The scorecard
`docs/scorecard.md`, generated by `cargo xtask scorecard` and committed like `docs/parity.md`. One section per area, each row with an id, a target, the measured value, a pass/fail state and a link to its issue.

| Area | How it's measured | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Performance | `cargo xtask perf`: a fixed set of benchmark scenarios (P1…Pn) with p50/p95 timings and peak RAM/GPU memory, compared against budgets in `perf/budgets.toml` and the last baseline | #209, #210, #211 |
| File compatibility | corpus pass and round-trip counts per corpus (ag-psd/psd-tools, psd-tools full, Photoshop-authored oracles, TIFF/RAW/EXR as they're added); per-format feature checklist | #215, #216, #190 |
| Tools | per-tool checklist: tool exists, live preview, honours mask/channel targets, Photoshop modifiers, tests | #213, #214, #207, #208 |
| Workspace and UI | checklist plus "settings that do nothing" count (must be 0) | #217, #204 |
| Type | checklist plus shaping golden tests per script | #218, #206 |
| Automation | share of UI actions reachable by command id; agent acceptance tasks passing | #219 |
| Reliability | `panic_hunt` green; atomic save; OOM injection; never-crash lint coverage | #203, #212 |
| Distribution | platforms and architectures shipped, update check | #220 |

## Done when
- [ ] `cargo xtask perf` runs the existing benches (`interactive_bench`, `layout_bench`, `fx_bench`, `large_image_bench`, ...) with `--json`, merges them into one result keyed by scenario id, and records machine, load average, commit and RSS in-process
- [ ] Budgets in `per…

title: Dropdown menus shouldn't have vertical scroll bars unless necessary
author: jlahijani
body:

title: GPU: arrow-key nudge in a 150-layer 20 MP document loses the device and panics
author: echelon
body:
Found by the perf scorecard (#239, scenario P12): pressing an arrow key to nudge a layer in a 150-layer, 20 MP document panics in `photocraft-gpu`:

```
Queue::write_buffer: Buffer with 'pc_compose_uniforms' label is invalid
```

(an earlier run failed with `pc_page_upload ... invalid` at unmap). It reproduces alone with `perf_scenarios --only nudge`; the 40-layer variant works. "Invalid buffer" after a large submission is the signature of a lost wgpu device (compare #128, where the first composite of a 174-layer layout lost the device; #226 fixes that case by bounding small layers' passes).

## Expected
- Nudging is fast (target ≤ 30 ms, #209) and never loses the device.
- If the device is lost anyway, the app must not panic: detect device loss, fall back to the CPU compositor (or recreate the device) and keep the document (never-crash rule).

## To do
- Re-run P12 after #226 lands; if it still reproduces, find which submission blows up (paged uploads? per-chunk passes?) and bound it.
- Device-lost handling: register `device.on_uncaptured_error` / lost callback, stop issuing GPU work, fall back to CPU, show a status message. Test with a forced device loss.

title: Compositor deadlock: effect-map OnceLock init re-entered via rayon work stealing (intermittent freeze)
author: echelon
body:
`effect_maps` in `crates/compose/src/lib.rs` (~1277) builds a layer's effect maps inside `slot.get_or_init(...)` (a `OnceLock`) while being called from the parallel per-tile render. The init closure itself runs rayon parallel work. While a worker waits for its own nested parallel jobs, rayon's work-stealing can hand it another tile of the **same layer**. That tile calls `effect_maps` with the same key and blocks in `get_or_init` on the lock that this very thread holds further up its stack. That is a permanent deadlock: 0% CPU, the app or test hangs forever.

Seen in `psd_tools_mutations_never_panic` (corpus sweep) hanging for 30+ minutes; a stack sample shows the threads parked in `OnceLock` wait at that line. It's intermittent (it depends on stealing order), so most runs pass. Any document with layer effects can hit it: a **user-facing freeze**.

## Fix
Never block on a once-init inside a rayon worker while the initializer can steal work. Options:
- Build the effect maps for all layers that need them **before** the parallel tile loop (a prepare pass), so tiles only read finished entries. This is preferred, and matches how patterns and vector masks are prepared once per render (#104/#112).
- Or make the cache non-blocking: `get()`; if empty, build outside the lock and `set()`, first one wins. This risks duplicate work, so it's only acceptable as a fallback.

## Test
A regression test that composites a layer with effects across many tiles on a small rayon pool, with nested parallelism forced (e.g. `ThreadPoolBuilder::num_threads(2)`), repeated many times under a timeout. It must never hang. Also run the corpus mutation sweep several times.

title: MCP `doc_inspect` ignores `index` in bridge mode
author: bekhruzbekswe
body:
MCP `doc_inspect` ignores `index` in bridge mode and always returns the active document.

**Version:** `photocraft-cli` 0.2.0, `mcp --bridge 127.0.0.1:<port>` connected to a running `photocraft --control <port>`

**Repro**
1. Open two documents in the app: A (index 0) and B (index 1, active).
2. Call `doc_inspect {"index": 0}`.
3. You get B back.

**Cause:** in bridge mode the tool sends `document.inspect` with empty params, so `p.index` is dropped:
https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/5ada60c/crates/automation/src/server.rs#L393-L401

The engine command already supports the argument (`document.inspect {"document": index?}`), so passing `{"document": p.index}` when it's set should fix it.

**Related (enhancement):** in bridge mode, `doc_select` and `doc_close` return "only available in headless mode". The engine's `document.activate {"document"}` and `file.close {"document"}` do the same thing over the control channel, so routing the tools through them would make MCP behave the same in both modes. As it stands, an agent's `doc_select` fails in bridge mode and its next command lands on the wrong document.

title: Fast brush strokes render as a coarse polyline (jagged curves)
author: leonaci
body: ## Summary Drawing with a **pen tablet** quickly produces visibly jagged, polygonal curves: the committed stroke is a coarse polyline of straight segments instead of a smooth curve. Slow strokes look fine. ## Environment - PhotoCraft 0.2.0, Windows, **pen tablet** (reproduced with a stylus, not a mouse) - Brush tool, default Hard Round, zoom ~100% ## Steps to reproduce 1. New document, select the Brush, and draw a fast spiral or circle with the pen in one quick motion. 2. Release. 3. The stroke is made of a handful of straight segments with sharp corners. ## Expected The stroke follows the pen smoothly, as in Photoshop. ## Actual The committed stroke is a polyline; the faster the stroke (or the lower the frame rate), the fewer the segments and the more angular it looks. The in-progress preview matches the committed result, so it is not just a preview artifact. A tablet reports at a high rate, so many samples are dropped per frame. ## Root cause - `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` reads `response.interact_pointer_pos()` **once per frame** while dragging, so only the pen's latest position reaches the tool. - egui-winit pushes one `egui::Event::PointerMoved` per winit `CursorMoved` (`on_cursor_moved` in egui-winit 0.36.2), and those accumulate in `InputState.events` when a frame is slow, so the intermediate samples are dropped. This is the same path for a mouse and a pen. - `crates/paint/src/dynamics.rs` `PathWalker` stamps dabs along straight segments between consecutive input points (no spline interpolation), so sparse samples give a polyline. The `Smoothing` option is an exponential lag filter and does not remove the corners. ## Related - #189 (closed) was about the *live preview* drawing a hard polygon; #240 made the preview equal the committed stroke, so the committed polyline itself remained. - #73 / #86 made `Smoothing` real. - …

title: Web: Liquify OK panics with "time not implemented on this platform" (std::time::Instant in distort_cmds.rs)
author: Biromedic
body:
## Summary

On the web build, clicking **OK** in Filter › Liquify panics with `time not implemented on this platform`. The app stops responding and any unsaved documents are lost.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft web build **v0.2.0** (`photocraft-web-0.2.0.zip` from the release, `photocraft-web-b33881c18c5db349_bg.wasm`), served as static files on `http://localhost:8765`
- Chrome 154 on Windows 11, WebGPU backend (`wgpu backend BrowserWebGpu`)
- Also reproduced in a second Chromium-based browser

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the web build and drop in any image (I used a 5184×3456 JPEG).
2. Filter › Liquify…
3. Make one Forward Warp stroke. The panel shows `1 stroke(s)` and the app is still responsive.
4. Click **OK**.

**Expected:** the warp is applied and the app keeps running.

**Actual:** the console shows

```
panicked at /rustc/b940084d7eb6a299eb4bfeb8e34901bc051e7ac4/library/std/src/sys/time/unsupported.rs:13:9:
time not implemented on this platform
...
Uncaught RuntimeError: unreachable
```

The frame loop stops (no further `requestAnimationFrame` calls) and the Liquify dialog stays on screen. Nothing responds, and reloading the page is the only way out. It happened 3 out of 3 times, including right after a fresh page load.

## Likely cause

`crates/engine/src/distort_cmds.rs`, in `fn liquify` (same code at the v0.2.0 tag and on current `main`):

```rust
let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
// ...
r["ms"] = json!(t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 1000.0);
```

`std::time::Instant::now()` panics on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. That fits what I saw: the stroke works, and the panic comes when the `filter.liquify` command runs on OK.

`photo_cmds.rs` already has a wasm-safe `Stopwatch` for this ("always 0 on the web, where `std::time::Instant` is unavailable"), so the fix is probably:

```rust
let t0 = crate::photo_cmds::Stopwatch::start();
// ...
r["ms"] = json!(t0.ms());
```

title: Cannot open PSB file larger than 4 GB: "The parameter is incorrect. (os error 87)"
author: HectorZaGa
body:
## Description
When trying to open a `.psb` (Photoshop Large Document Format) file that is larger than 4 GB, the app fails with the following error:

```
Couldn't open document.psb: The parameter is incorrect. (os error 87)
```

(`ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` on Windows.)

Smaller PSB files open without problems. The issue seems to appear only when the file exceeds 4 GB, which suggests a 32-bit size/offset limit somewhere in the file reading or memory mapping code.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Launch the app.
2. Open a `.psb` file larger than 4 GB (File > Open or drag and drop).
3. The error dialog appears and the file is not opened.

## Expected behavior
The file opens correctly, as PSB is designed to support files larger than 4 GB (up to 4 exabytes).

## Actual behavior
The file fails to open with `os error 87`.

## Environment
- App version: 0.2.0
- OS: Windows 11 (64-bit)
- File size: 4.75 GB
- File source: saved from Adobe Photoshop 2026
- Language of the OS: Spanish

## Additional context
- Smaller `.psb` files open fine: yes, I was able to open a 759 MB `.psb` file without issues.
- I can share a sample file if needed.

title: Linux Wayland: dropping files on the window does nothing (winit 0.30 has no Wayland drag and drop)
author: Ar-maan05
body:
## Problem

On a Wayland session, dragging an image from a file manager onto PhotoCraft does nothing: no hover feedback, no open, no error. This is the drag-and-drop half of #338 (reported on Hyprland). It also affects Fedora Workstation and Ubuntu, whose default session is GNOME on Wayland.

## Cause

`main.rs` enables `.with_drag_and_drop(true)` and `lib.rs` handles `raw.dropped_files`. But winit 0.30.13 (from eframe 0.36) only produces `WindowEvent::DroppedFile` / `HoveredFile` in its X11 backend (`platform_impl/linux/x11/event_processor.rs`). Its Wayland backend has no drag-and-drop support, so egui never receives the files. When eframe picks Wayland, which it does whenever `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set, drops are lost.

Workaround today: run under XWayland with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY= photocraft`. Drag and drop works there, at the cost of fractional scaling quality and native Wayland input.

## Environment

PhotoCraft 0.2.0 (RPM) and main at 909efc0, Fedora 44, GNOME 50 Wayland, x86_64.

## Possible directions

1. Wait for winit to add Wayland drag and drop upstream, then bump.
2. Offer an "X11 (XWayland)" display preference on Linux. It would apply at the next launch by unsetting `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` before eframe starts, like the GPU backend preference does.
3. At least tell the user: on Wayland, show a one-time hint ("drag and drop needs X11; use File > Open, Ctrl+V on a copied file, or ...") so the drop doesn't silently fail.

The paste half of #338 (Ctrl+V on a file copied in a file manager) is fixed separately in #<paste PR number>.

title: PSD save rewrites layer locks: Photoshop's lspf bit 3 (0x08) is dropped, and the artboard lock is written as 0x10
author: EthanSuquet
body:
**Version:** photocraft-cli 0.2.0, main @ 909efc0 · macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6), Apple M2 Max, release build

### What happens

Opening a Photoshop PSD and saving it again (`photocraft-cli convert in.psd out.psd`, no edits) changes the
`lspf` (layer protection) block of every Background layer from `0x0000000D` to `0x00000005`.
Layers locked with Lock All change from `0x80000000` to `0x80000001`.

`crates/io/src/blocks.rs:48-58` maps the artboard lock to `0x10` ("bit 3 … here 0x10 as observed by
ag-psd": bit 3 is `0x08`, so the comment contradicts itself). Photoshop writes `0x08`: across the pinned
public corpora (`cargo xtask corpus --all`: photocraft-corpus, psd-tools, ag-psd) there are 336 `lspf`
blocks with `0x0D`, 37 with `0x05`, 1 with `0x07`, and none with `0x10`. So bit 3 is read as nothing and
written back as 0, and a lock set in PhotoCraft is written as a bit Photoshop doesn't use.

The Lock All change comes from the record's transparency-protected flag being folded into the locks on
import (`psd_import.rs` ~line 203). That one may be fine, but it means no Photoshop file with Lock All
saves back byte for byte.

### Repro (public corpus file)

1. `cargo xtask corpus --all`
2. `photocraft-cli convert corpus/photoshop/smart-filters/sf-add-noise-gaussian-mono-20-seed.psd out.psd`
3. Read the Background layer's `lspf` from both files.

**Expected:** `0x0000000D` (unchanged). **Actual:** `0x00000005`.

### Suggested fix

Use `0x08` for `Locks::artboard` in `locks_from_lspf` / `lspf_from_locks`, and accept `0x10` on read for
files PhotoCraft wrote before. Update `locks_and_labels` to the Photoshop values (`0x0D` round trip).

title: feat(automation): keep headless saves without `path` from flattening over the opened file
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

In headless automation (`photocraft-cli mcp` without `--bridge`, and `photocraft-cli serve`), a save that omits `path` writes over the file the document was opened from, even when the written format is flat. `doc_save {}` on a document opened from a PNG or JPEG replaces it with a flattened export, recompressed for JPEG, and `doc_save {"format":"png"}` on a layered PSD replaces the PSD with PNG bytes under the `.psd` name. The desktop's File › Save sends flat documents to Save As so they are "not silently flattened over the original", and MCP `doc_save` in bridge mode refuses a missing `path`. This asks headless saves without `path` to give the opened file the same protection.

## Problem to solve

The `path` field of MCP `doc_save` documents the fallback ("Omit to save to the document's own relative path"), `docs/control-protocol.md` lists `doc.save` for `serve` as `{path?, format?, quality?, index?}`, and the reply lists warnings such as "2 layer(s) flattened; layers, masks and blend modes are not kept" and "lossy compression". The warnings arrive after the original has been replaced, so a client cannot act on them. The MCP tool description reads "Save the document", and the server instructions point clients at `doc_save` for saving, so an agent that saves its work without `path` replaces the user's input file. A JPEG is re-encoded even when nothing was edited. The desktop app treats this as something to avoid: `file.save` saves in place only for `.psd`, `.psb` and `.pcraft` (`saves_in_place` in `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`), and the test `pcraft_documents_save_in_place_but_flat_files_ask` in `crates/ui-egui/src/file_open/tests.rs` states that a PNG "goes through Save As (cancelled here), not silently flattened over the original". Headless automation applies no such rule.

## Proposed behavior

title: [Bug] Rapid Undo followed by Save drops Undo
author: Jagalite
body:
## Environment

- Revision: `a0d49de0478fbaa91733517297432e7bbe5b479f`
- macOS, Apple M1
- Chromium 152.0.7977.130 in the T3 collaborative browser
- WebGPU backend

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a 128×128 white PSD with a red 32×32 square in the upper-left corner.
2. Select a rectangle in the white area and fill it black.
3. Send **Command+Z**, immediately followed by **Command+S**, without an intervening rendered frame. **Undo events arrive first, then Save events.**
4. Inspect the downloaded PSD.
5. Wait, save again, and inspect that download.
6. Repeat with a pause between Undo and Save as a control.

The same-frame timing matters; pressing the shortcuts manually may deliver them in separate frames.

## Expected

Undo removes the black fill. Both downloads contain the restored image.

## Actual

The rapid sequence saved the black fill in two attempts. Saving again after a delay still retained it. When Undo and Save were separated by rendered frames, the saved image restored every original pixel.

## Impact

The saved document can retain an edit the user requested to undo.

## Scope

Reproduced with automated browser input. Delivering both shortcuts in one input frame of the native headless shared UI also reproduced the problem; separate frames worked. This points to shared shortcut handling, not a Wasm-specific issue.

Physical keyboard delivery has not been verified. The behavior has not been rechecked on revisions newer than the one above.

## Suspected cause

The shortcut dispatcher selects one matching binding per frame in binding order, rather than processing both shortcuts in event order.

title: [Bug] Image Size accepts zero width with a preview that disagrees with the saved dimensions

## Suspected cause

The dialog's validation/preview and the engine's minimum-dimension normalization appear inconsistent.

title: [Bug] A second crash can lose recovered unsaved documents
author: Jagalite
body:
## Environment

- Revision: `a0d49de0478fbaa91733517297432e7bbe5b479f`
- macOS, Apple M1
- Native application / command routes as specified below

## Steps to reproduce

Use a dedicated app instance with a fresh `PHOTOCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` and disposable documents.

1. Enable `fileHandling.autosave` and `fileHandling.recoverOnLaunch`; set `fileHandling.autosaveMinutes` to `1`.
2. Create two unsaved 4×4 documents, one filled red and one blue.
3. Wait until both recovery bundles and their JSON sidecars have been written.
4. Force-terminate the app, then restart it with the same configuration.
5. Confirm both documents recover and remain marked as unsaved.
6. Before the next autosave, force-terminate the app again and restart it.

## Expected

Recovered unsaved documents remain recoverable after a second crash. Their durable recovery copies should survive until a replacement snapshot or explicit save/discard safely supersedes them.

## Actual

The first recovery restores both documents and their pixels correctly, but the recovery directory is already empty afterward. A second termination approximately 0.70 seconds after inspecting the recovered documents leaves zero documents on the next launch. Repeating from preserved recovery snapshots reproduced the loss.

## Impact

Unsaved work that successfully survived one crash can be lost after a second crash before the next autosave.

## Scope

Confirmed twice in the native macOS application. Browser/Wasm and other operating systems are unverified. The behavior has not been rechecked on newer revisions.

## Suspected cause

Native recovery services discard recovery entries immediately after loading them, while replacement autosaves are scheduled after the configured interval. This leaves a gap with no durable recovery copy.

## Request

## Environment

title: bug(cli): paint.gradient ignores explicit transparency stops in v0.2.0
author: njrun1804
body:
PhotoCraft v0.2.0 macOS universal CLI, macOS 27.0.1. Reproduced with a synthetic 16×16 document; no external images required.

The `commands --json` registry advertises `transparency: [[t,0..100], …]` for `paint.gradient`. Passing explicit transparency stops returns success, but the exported gradient is fully opaque.

### Reproduce

```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":16,"height":16,"background":"transparent"}'   --cmd paint.gradient   --params '{"from":[0,0],"to":[0,15],"colors":["#07111d","#07111d"],"transparency":[[0,65],[1,0]]}'   --out gradient.png
```

Expected: dark blue with an alpha ramp from approximately 65% to 0%.

Observed: exit 0, `{"command":"paint.gradient","result":null}`. The PNG has RGB color type 2 (no alpha channel), and its top and bottom pixels are both `[7,17,29]`: fully opaque.

Control: the same operation with `"opacity":35` instead of `transparency` produces RGBA color type 6, alpha 89 throughout, so transparency of the initial document and PNG export work.

Workaround confirmed: paint the gradient into a separate layer mask using `target:"mask"` with white/black colors, then set layer opacity.

I have only reproduced this against the published v0.2.0 CLI, not built current main.

title: bug(cli): smartFilter.setParams rejects explicit smart-object target when adjustment layer is active
author: njrun1804
body:
PhotoCraft v0.2.0 macOS universal CLI, macOS 27.0.1. Synthetic 16×16 document; no external images required.

The registry advertises an optional explicit `layer` target for `layer.smartFilter.setParams`, but the command is rejected when the active layer is an adjustment, even when the requested target is a valid smart object with a filter.

### Reproduce

```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":16,"height":16,"background":"white"}'   --cmd layer.smartObjects.convertToSmartObject   --cmd filter.sharpen.smartSharpen --params '{"amount":65,"radius":1}'   --cmd layer.newAdjustmentLayer.curves --params '{"points":[[0,0],[255,255]]}'   --out repro.pcraft
```

In this run, the smart object is layer 4 and the active Curves adjustment is layer 5 (confirmed with `photocraft-cli info repro.pcraft --compact`).

```sh
photocraft-cli run repro.pcraft   --cmd layer.smartFilter.setParams   --params '{"layer":4,"index":0,"params":{"amount":80}}'   --out changed.pcraft
```

Expected: update the filter on explicitly targeted layer 4, regardless of the active layer.

Observed: exit 1:

```text
error: `layer.smartFilter.setParams`: command `layer.smartFilter.setParams` is not available right now: the active layer is a Adjustment layer, not a smart object
```

Control/workaround: insert `--cmd layer.select --params '{"layer":4}'` before `setParams`. The same operation then succeeds, returning `{"layer":4}`. This confirms that the target smart object and saved filter are valid.

Could the availability check resolve the explicit target, or could the documented contract be clarified if active-layer selection is intentionally required?

I have only reproduced this against the published v0.2.0 CLI, not built current main.

title: [Bug] Browser tab overwrites unrelated preferences changed in another tab
author: Jagalite
body:
## Environment

- Revision: `2620460267933c4a04717465f50641f5d4f820a2`
- Release browser/Wasm build, served locally over HTTP
- macOS, Apple M1
- Google Chrome 154.0.8037.93, headless
- Playwright Firefox 155.0, headless
- Playwright WebKit 26.6, headless (not Safari)
- Default backend: WebGPU in Chrome/WebKit; WebGL2 in Firefox because WebGPU was blocklisted

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the browser app in two tabs, A and B, sharing the same origin and storage. Start with the default theme in both.
2. In tab A, change the theme using the toolbar appearance button. The stored theme changes from `proMedium` to `studio`.
3. Without reloading tab B, use File > Open to import a valid GRD gradient preset. The reproduced case uses one opaque red-to-blue gradient.
4. Inspect `photocraft.preferences` in localStorage, then reload tab A.

## Expected

The imported gradient is saved without changing the theme selected in tab A.

## Actual

The gradient is saved, but the stored theme changes back from `studio` to `proMedium`. Reloading A shows the old theme. This reproduces in all three browsers.

## Impact

An unrelated action in another tab silently loses a saved preference change.

## Scope

This is a browser shared-storage conflict, not merely a lack of live theme synchronization. No native equivalent was checked. The result applies to the revision above; newer revisions have not been rechecked.

## Suspected cause

Each tab writes its entire in-memory preference snapshot without reconciling changes made by other tabs.

title: [Bug] Browser does not retry saving preferences after a transient storage failure
author: Jagalite
body:
## Environment

- Revision: `2620460267933c4a04717465f50641f5d4f820a2`
- Release browser/Wasm build, served locally over HTTP
- macOS, Apple M1
- Google Chrome 154.0.8037.93, headless
- Playwright Firefox 155.0, headless
- Playwright WebKit 26.6, headless (not Safari)
- Default backend: WebGPU in Chrome/WebKit; WebGL2 in Firefox because WebGPU was blocklisted

## Steps to reproduce

1. Change the theme and reload once to confirm that preferences persist normally.
2. In the page context, temporarily inject a storage-write failure:

```js
window.originalSetItem = Storage.prototype.setItem;
Storage.prototype.setItem = function () {
  throw new DOMException("Injected quota failure", "QuotaExceededError");
};
```

3. Change the theme again. Observe the preference-save error.
4. Restore storage writes:

```js
Storage.prototype.setItem = window.originalSetItem;
```

5. Wait three seconds without changing another preference, then reload.
6. As a control, make a fresh preference change after reloading.

## Expected

A failed write remains pending, with a retry path once storage works again, rather than being treated internally as successfully persisted.

## Actual

The app displays the initial error, but no retry is observed during the three-second wait. Reload restores the old theme. A fresh edit saves successfully once storage works. Reproduced in all three browsers.

## Impact

A preference change remains unsaved after a transient storage failure has been removed and is lost on reload.

## Scope

This uses controlled `QuotaExceededError` injection; naturally exhausted storage was not reproduced. The observation is bounded to the wait above, not a claim that every possible later action fails to retry. Newer revisions have not been rechecked.

## Suspected cause

In `crates/ui-egui/src/prefs_ui.rs`, the saved preference revision advances before the storage callback succeeds, so the failed revision no longer appears pending.

title: fix(cli): batch --actions rejects the [id, params] steps that recorded actions and droplets use
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`photocraft-cli batch --actions <file>` accepts only `{"command": id, "params": {…}}` objects as steps. A step written as an `[id, params]` pair, which is how a recorded action stores its steps and how `file.automate.createDroplet` writes them, fails with `error: action 0: missing "command"` and exit 1 before any image is processed. The engine's own batch command, `file.automate.batch`, runs the same steps without error. The development guide describes the `--actions` file as "the same shape as a recorded action", so a step list copied from a recorded action or a droplet cannot be used with `batch`.

## Runtime or environment

- Release build: `photocraft-cli 0.2.0 (ad8632173, 2026-10-05)`, the v0.2.0 release CLI, on macOS 27.0 arm64.
- Source build: `main` at 93bd44899baf17f28f48ca47a652fb2dd5db2821. The one later commit on `main` at the time of testing, a0997942d33abbab1be645eeae0cab41866bf011, changes no file under `apps/photocraft-cli` or `crates/automation`.
- Both builds behave identically for every step below.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create two small inputs and three action files (any images work; these use ffmpeg):

```sh

ffmpeg -v error -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=64x48 -frames:v 1 in/a.png
```

title: fix(cli): --quality accepts 0 and 101-255 silently but rejects 256 and above
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The CLI documents `--quality <1-100>` for `convert`, `run` and `batch`. Values 0 and 101 through 255 are accepted without an error and clamped into 1-100, while 256 and above are rejected with ``error: bad --quality `256` `` and exit 1, like negative or non-numeric values. Which out-of-range values are errors depends on the parser's integer type rather than on the documented range.

## Runtime or environment

- Release build: `photocraft-cli 0.2.0 (ad8632173, 2026-10-05)`, the v0.2.0 release CLI, on macOS 27.0 arm64.
- Source build: `main` at 93bd44899baf17f28f48ca47a652fb2dd5db2821. The one later commit on `main` at the time of testing, a0997942d33abbab1be645eeae0cab41866bf011, changes no file under `apps/photocraft-cli` or `crates/automation`.
- Both builds behave identically for steps 1 and 2 below; step 3 was run on the `main` build only.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a small PNG, an input folder and an action file (any image works; this uses ffmpeg):

```sh
ffmpeg -v error -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=64x48 -frames:v 1 a.png
mkdir in && cp a.png in/
echo '[{"command":"image.adjustments.invert"}]' > act.json
```

2. For each value `0 1 50 100 101 255 256 1000 -1 abc`, delete `q.jpg`, run `photocraft-cli convert a.png q.jpg --quality <value>`, and record the exit status and the size of `q.jpg` if it exists.
3. Run `photocraft-cli run a.png --cmd image.adjustments.invert --out r.jpg --quality 0` and `photocraft-cli batch --actions act.json --in in --out qb --format jpg --quality 300`, recording each exit status.

## Expected behavior

The usage text declares the accepted range as `--quality <1-100>`, and the CLI already rejects some values outside it with ``bad --quality `<value>` ``. Every integer outside 1-100 should therefore be rejected with that error and write no file. Whether a value outside the documented range is an error should not depend on whether it fits in 8 bits.
