title: Vanishing Point: tear off perpendicular planes and the Stamp tool (TOOL-214-14)
author: vangel76
body:
Follow-up to #3122 / #3133 (on-canvas Vanishing Point plane editor).

The Vanishing Point window can draw and edit planes and paste onto them, but two parts of Photoshop's window are still missing:

- **Tear off planes:** Ctrl/Cmd-dragging an edge node should tear off a perpendicular plane (90° by default). Dragging the new plane's far edge node sets its depth, and Alt-dragging it sets its angle. The torn plane should follow its parent and reach `filter.vanishingPoint` as `{"from", "edge", "angle", "depth"}`.
- **Stamp tool (S):** Alt-clicking a plane should set the source, and painting should clone in perspective (Diameter, Hardness, Opacity, Aligned) with a live preview. The strokes should be applied on OK as the command's `clone` param, so the whole session is one history step.

The engine already supports torn-off planes and perspective clone strokes. Its `clone` param still needs input validation and caps (stroke and point counts, finite numbers).

Out of scope: the window's Marquee tool and the Stamp's Heal modes (Off/Luminance/On). The engine has no heal mode yet.

Scorecard row: TOOL-214-14.

On `main` a smart object's filter mask can only come from the selection when the first smart filter is added (`smart_cmds.rs` `add_smart_filter`). It can't be targeted or painted afterwards:

- `paint.stroke` and the other pixel commands have no filter-mask target. On a smart object without a layer mask they're refused ("active layer is a Smart Object layer without a mask").

Photoshop: clicking the filter mask thumbnail targets it. The painting tools, fills, filters and adjustments then edit it (black hides the smart filters there), with one undo step per stroke. ⌥-click shows the mask alone and ⇧-click disables it. The mask already persists through .pcraft and PSD (`FEid`).

title: The saved manifest keeps the previous document name
author: weavebrain
body:
## Summary

After a successful Save As to a new filename, the document's in-session name is
updated correctly, but the name written into the saved `.pcraft` manifest is the
**originally opened** document's name. Reopening the saved file shows the old
name, so the tab and the file disagree.

This looks like the persistence half of #2018 ("Update document names after
successful Save As"). #2018 correctly fixed the in-session identity; the
serialised manifest name does not appear to be covered.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft **0.7.0** (macOS universal), headless CLI + `serve`
- Reproduced 2026-10-11

## Steps to reproduce

Using the headless server (`photocraft-cli serve`), with a document on disk
named `FirstTest.psd`:

```json
{"id":1,"method":"doc.open","params":{"path":"build/FirstTest.psd"}}
{"id":2,"method":"doc.save","params":{"path":"build/_nametest.pcraft"}}
{"id":3,"method":"doc.inspect"}
```

Then reopen the file that was just written:

```json
{"id":1,"method":"doc.open","params":{"path":"build/_nametest.pcraft"}}
{"id":2,"method":"doc.inspect"}
```

Also reproducible via `photocraft-cli run <in> --cmd <id> --out <new-name>.pcraft`.

## Expected

The saved document reports `_nametest.pcraft` — matching the filename it was
saved to, and matching what the session reported immediately after saving.

## Actual

```
after doc.save,  doc.inspect  ->  name = "_nametest.pcraft"   (correct, in-session)
reopen the file, doc.inspect  ->  name = "FirstTest.psd"      (stale)
photocraft-cli info <file>    ->  name = "FirstTest.psd"      (stale)

manifest.json:  document.name = "FirstTest.psd"
```

So the in-memory identity adopts the basename, but the manifest writer
serialises the previous name.

## Scope

Reproduced on both headless save paths (`run --out` and `doc.save`), so it
appears to be in the manifest serialisation rather than one call site.

**Not tested:** GUI `File > Save As`. I can't say whether the GUI shares the
defect or already persists correctly — worth …

title: Range ignores the active selection and samples the entire canvas instead of the selected region
author: showoffing
body: When a selection is active and Color Range is invoked, the tool should sample colors only within that selection and constrain the resulting selection to it. The active selection should act as a mask for color sampling. In PhotoCraft, the active selection is ignored. Color Range samples the entire canvas regardless, and the resulting selection extends beyond the original selection boundary. This makes the tool unusable for targeted color edits on a specific region — the exact workflow it exists for. Expected: With an active selection, Color Range should sample and select only within that selection. Actual: The active selection is discarded. Color Range samples the full canvas, and the result is not constrained to the original selection. Relevant context: The release notes list Color Range as implemented ("the dialog, Select presets, eyedroppers, Localized Color Clusters, Invert") , and v0.6.0 includes "improve previews, sampling and eyedropper responsiveness" for Color Range . However, the selection-scoping behavior is either missing or not wired into the sampling path. The scorecard also notes only partial test coverage for Sampled Colors at Fuzziness 0

title: Format: .pcraft load decodes shared tiles once per reference, so large solid documents don't reopen
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

`.pcraft` saves deduplicate tiles by content hash (a solid fill shares one `Arc<Tile>` across the whole canvas, #705), but loading decodes every tile *reference* separately and charges each one against `max_total_bytes` (16 GiB). Two consequences on `main`:

1. **Large solid documents don't reopen.** `file.new` 300000×300000 (white background) saves fine, but `load_from_bytes` fails with `LimitExceeded("bundle expands beyond 17179869184 bytes")`: 1.37 M references × 256 KiB. The threshold is reached far earlier at higher depths: an RGBA canvas filled with one colour stops reopening at about 65536² (8-bit), 46341² (16-bit) or 32768² (32-bit float), all sizes `file.new` allows.
2. **Reopening loses tile sharing.** Below the limit every reference gets its own decoded tile, so a solid 30000×30000 32-bit document takes about 14 GB of RAM after reopening, versus about 1 MB when it was created.

## Where

- `crates/format/src/store.rs` `LoadFetch::tile`: `self.account(len)` + decompress + hash check per call, no cache by hash (unlike `LoadFetch::blob`, which caches).
- `crates/format/src/convert.rs` `Loader::surface`: `s.tile_mut(c).bytes_mut().copy_from_slice(&bytes)` gives every coordinate its own tile.

## Expected

Whatever saves must reopen (the same principle as #2935): identical tile hashes should be decoded and charged once and shared as one `Arc<Tile>` (copy-on-write), so reopening costs what the file holds, not what the canvas spans.

## Repro

```rust
let mut s = Session::new();
s.execute("file.new", json!({"width": 300000, "height": 300000})).unwrap();
let bytes = photocraft_format::save_to_bytes(&s.active().unwrap().doc, &Default::default()).unwrap();
photocraft_format::load_from_bytes(&bytes).unwrap(); // LimitExceeded("bundle expands beyond 17179869184 bytes")
```

Found while making the `.pcraft` canvas admission match `file.new` (#3295).

title: [Better Than PS] Free Warp, Distort and Perspective on live type, which stays editable
author: vangel76
body:
Photoshop limits what you can do to live type:
- **Edit › Transform › Warp** gives you only the preset warp styles (Warp Text). You can't drag the mesh.
- **Distort**, **Perspective** and the split warps are greyed until you rasterize the type, and then the text can no longer be edited.

Wish: do all of these without rasterizing.
- Warp on a type layer lets you drag and split the mesh freely, as on pixels and Smart Objects.
- Distort and Perspective are enabled for type.
- The result stays on the type layer as a non-destructive transform. The text stays editable: editing it re-renders under the same warp or distort. Each transform is one undo step, and moving, scaling or rotating the layer afterwards carries it along.
- It is saved in `.pcraft`.
- PSD export: Photoshop can't store a custom warp or a quad on type. Such a layer is written as an embedded Smart Object holding the live type layer, with the warp/quad as the Smart Object's transform. It then looks right in Photoshop and stays editable via Edit Contents. Type without these transforms exports exactly as before.

This builds on #3004 / #3008 (Warp on type takes the warp styles, as in Photoshop).

title: [Bug]: Installed system fonts do not appear in the Text Tool font picker
author: LimitlessRam
body:
## Description

On the Windows portable build in the test video, the Horizontal Type font dropdown does not list an installed family such as Futura. Only a small set is shown. Impact is one face that does appear.

## What is already true

Per-user fonts in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts` have been scanned since ae92ac20 (2026-09-30). That commit is in every release from v0.1.0 through v0.7.0, so a public portable zip is not missing that folder.

On v0.7.0, `system_font_dirs()` in `crates/text/src/fonts.rs` only reads directories:

- `%WINDIR%\Fonts`
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts`

It does not call DirectWrite, and it does not read the font registry. A family Windows can draw, whose file is not in those two folders, never appears. Adobe Fonts (Creative Cloud) and font managers that activate fonts from another directory are in that set.

## What this report does not record

The source video does not say where Futura came from, and it does not show Help › About.

- Video: https://youtu.be/Oc51Ty9h-68?t=796 (chapter "Font Issues in PhotoCraft", 13:13)
- Published 2026-10-10 by Tech It Before You Wreck It
- Described as a 64MB Windows portable build

The written steps say the font was placed in a standard OS font directory and worked in Notepad, Word, or Photoshop. If that file was in `C:\Windows\Fonts` or the per-user Fonts folder on v0.5.0 or newer, the directory scan should have found a `.ttf`, `.otf`, `.ttc`, or `.otc`, and this would still be a bug. The install path and the build version were not recorded, so that case cannot be reproduced from this report.

## Still missing

Fonts that Windows lists, and whose files live outside the two directories above.

## Environment

- App: Windows portable 64-bit. Version not recorded.
- OS: Windows 10 / 11 (64-bit)
- Formats mentioned: `.otf`, `.ttf`

title: Tests: 'bad layer id' sentinels like 9999 can collide with real ids from the global counter (flaky CI)
author: vangel76
body:
`photocraft-engine`'s lib test `type_extra_cmds::tests::vertical_orientation_renders_columns_inside_the_canvas` fails on CI at random:

```
assertion failed: s.execute("type.orientation.vertical", json!({"layer": 9999})).is_err()
crates/engine/src/type_extra_cmds/tests.rs:112
```

It passes when run alone.

**Cause:** layer ids come from one process-wide counter (`NEXT_ID` in `crates/doc/src/lib.rs`, shared by `LayerId`, `DocId` and `SmartContentsId`, and pushed up further by `ensure_ids_above` whenever a test loads a file). `cargo test` runs all of the ~thousands of lib tests in one process, so the counter passes 9999 during a normal run. If a layer that the test itself just created happens to get id 9999, the "bad" id names a real layer, the command succeeds and the assertion fails. Which test gets that id depends on thread scheduling, so the failure jumps between PRs.

Many tests use the same pattern with small sentinels (`"layer": 9999`, `999_999`, `99999`, `LayerId(9999)`, `"reference": 9999`, `"to": 9999` …) in `crates/engine` and `crates/ui-egui`. Any of them can flake the same way.

**Fix:** use an id the counter can never reach (`u64::MAX`) in these "no such layer" checks. The change is test-only.

title: CI: let first-time contributors' PRs run without approval
author: 1Git2Clone
body:
Fork PRs from anyone without a merged PR here wait for a maintainer to approve their workflow runs ("Require approval for first-time contributors", GitHub's default). On a repo with this many newcomers that's a real queue: of the last 400 CI runs on pull requests (since 2026-10-10 23:52 UTC), **108 are waiting for approval**, from 23 different people, and 1,051 runs across all workflows sit at `action_required`. A newcomer gets no feedback on their first PR until a maintainer does a pass, and each new push needs approving again.

## Proposal

Settings › Actions › General › *Approval for running fork pull request workflows from contributors*: switch from **"Require approval for first-time contributors"** to **"Require approval for first-time contributors who are new to GitHub"**. Brand-new accounts, where CI abuse (crypto miners, spam) comes from, still wait for approval; established accounts making their first contribution get CI right away.

## Why it's safe

- Fork PRs run on `pull_request`, so they get **no secrets** and a **read-only** `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The only workflow with secrets, `release.yml`, runs on push/tag, never on PRs. Nothing uses `pull_request_target`.
- Every job runs on a fresh VM that's thrown away afterwards.
- PR runs can't write main's caches; they write only to their own PR scope (and with #2933 not at all).
- Worst case, a burst of abusive PRs from established accounts ties up runners until the runs are cancelled. Interaction limits (PRs from prior contributors only) stop a wave in one click, and GitHub suspends mining accounts under its terms.

## Hardening to go with it (small PR)

- `permissions: contents: read` at the top of `ci.yml`. It has none, so main and same-repo PR runs get the repo's default token permissions.
- `persist-credentials: false` on checkouts that don't push.
- Third-party actions in `ci.yml` pinned by commit SHA, like #2270 and #2939 propose for the release workflows.

One thing a maintainer could check at the same tim…

title: Let an end user add a font without rebuilding
author: tonguyenducmanh
body:
## Ask

Let an end user add a font without rebuilding:

- **Paste a link** — Google Fonts `/css2?family=…`, any stylesheet with `@font-face`, or a direct
  `.ttf` / `.otf` / `.woff2` URL.
- **Upload a file** — drag-drop or picker.

Today that requires a source edit, so users of a released web build can't do it at all.

## Current behaviour

PhotoCraft is the closest of the four to this already:

- `crates/text/src/served.rs` parses `fonts/manifest.txt` and owns the fetch queue
  (`add_fonts`, `request_for_text`, `request_for_languages`).
- `apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs:29` fetches that file **next to `index.html`**.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/cjk_fonts.rs` already scans each frame for uncovered glyphs and registers
  the next candidate font.

So the only gap is that the catalog comes from a **host-provided file** rather than from the
**user**.

## Suggestion

- Reuse `served::fetch` (already `AbortController` + timeout + `array_buffer()`) with a different
  URL — no manifest needed for a direct link.
- Make user-installed fonts candidates in the existing `cjk_fonts.rs` scanner, so they help text
  that already has missing glyphs instead of only text the user retypes with a font picked by hand.
- Use `script_fallbacks` for "which scripts does this font cover".

## Why this fits

Four entries in the `CommandSpec` registry, and the web UI, CLI, MCP surface and JSON control
channel all follow for free:

| id | params |
| --- | --- |
| `font.install_url` | `{ url }` — `journal: true` |
| `font.install_file` | `{ path }` (desktop) / `rfd` picker (web) |
| `font.remove` | `{ family }` |
| `font.list` | — |

Persist in IndexedDB (`localStorage`'s ~5 MB is smaller than one CJK face); on desktop, the app
font directory `FontDb` already scans. Per `standards/never-crash.md`: unreachable URL, timeout or
non-font file → log and skip, never panic; keep `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, …)]` green.

## Acceptance criteria

- Installed font appears in the existing font menus, on a **stock…

title: Feature: Blue “Saving” progress bar in the status bar (Ctrl+S)
author: mode0192
body:
## Description

In Photoshop, when you press **Ctrl+S** (especially with background save), two progress indicators appear:

1. **Bottom status bar**: a blue progress bar that says “Saving 99%” (with a cancel button). A separate percentage readout is also shown to the left of the bar.
2. **Document tab**: the tab title also shows the progress as text, e.g. `… RGB/16) - Saving 99%`.

PhotoCraft currently shows no live progress while saving. A short note only appears at the bottom right after the save has already finished.

## Expected behavior

- When saving (Ctrl+S / File → Save), show a blue progress bar in the lower status bar that says “Saving XX%”, matching Photoshop.
- Also show the percentage in the document tab title (as Photoshop does).
- For larger files, the save should preferably run in the background so the UI stays responsive while the indicators are visible.
- Both indicators should disappear once the save completes.

## Current behavior

No progress is shown while the save is in progress. The only feedback is a note that appears after the save finishes.

## Motivation

The blue “Saving” bar (and the matching text in the tab) is a clear, familiar visual cue that the document is being saved. It is especially useful for large or layered files and matches existing Photoshop muscle memory.

## Notes

- Related: #210 (background jobs with progress) and the closed #2017 (large saves blocking the UI with no progress).
- A simple status-bar progress indicator would already be a big improvement even before full background-save support.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft version: 0.7.0

title: Automation: a way to give a headless session a font file or folder
author: HassanJb961
body:
**Version:** PhotoCraft 0.7.0 (792616159, 2026-10-11), `photocraft-0.7.0-windows-x64-portable.zip`, Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200.

**Problem**

A headless session sees the bundled fonts and the fonts installed on the machine, and nothing else. I found no way to add one:

- `engine.commands {"filter":"font"}` lists only `type.fonts`, `type.resolveMissingFonts` and `type.replaceAllMissingFonts`.
- `photocraft-cli --help` has no font option.
- A path is taken as a family name. With `fonts/Tajawal-Bold.ttf` inside the read root, `type.create {"font":"fonts/Tajawal-Bold.ttf"}` and `type.create {"font":"Tajawal"}` both succeed, and `type.resolveMissingFonts` then lists both as missing.

**Use case**

Scripted layouts where the typefaces travel with the project as .ttf files instead of being installed: a brand's fonts in a repository, a CI job, a container, an agent's sandbox. Today the output depends on what happens to be installed on that machine.

**Workaround today**

On Windows the scan reads `%WINDIR%\Fonts` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts` (`system_font_dirs` in `crates/text/src/fonts.rs`). Starting the server with `LOCALAPPDATA` pointed at a private folder that holds `Microsoft\Windows\Fonts\*.ttf` makes those fonts visible. It works, including variable-font weights and Arabic shaping, but it is a hack and it hides the user's own per-user fonts from that session.

**Request**

One of:

1. A flag, for example `--font-dir <dir>` (repeatable) on `serve`, `mcp`, `run`, `batch` and `convert`, scanned in addition to the system folders.
2. Or a scoped method, for example `fonts.register {path}` (MCP: `fonts_register`), resolving a file or folder under the read root and handing the bytes to the existing `register_font_data`.

Either way `type.fonts` should list what was added.

Related: #1251 (missing-font warnings).

title: Actions: replay tests for crop, filters, selections and styled text on a second document (AUTO-219-4)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #219 (scorecard AUTO-219-4, docs/gaps.md G11).

## What's missing on main
Replay coverage for actions is thin: `crates/engine/src/actions_cmds.rs` tests replay a new layer + rect select + fill (`play_on_another_document_matches_pixels_at_each_depth`) and an explicit/again transform. Nothing checks that a recorded action with a **crop**, a **filter**, **selection operations** or a **styled type layer** replays on a second document and produces the same result as running those commands directly.

## Photoshop behaviour
Playing an action runs its recorded commands, in order, against the active document, which need not be the one it was recorded on ([Adobe: Creating actions](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/using/creating-actions.html), [Playing and managing actions](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/using/playing-managing-actions.html)).

## Proposal
Tests only (new integration test file `crates/engine/tests/action_replay.rs`, no command changes):
- record on document A via `actions.record` / `actions.stop`, open a fresh document B, `actions.play`, and compare B against a document C on which the same commands were executed directly (oracle: pixels, layer count/kinds, selection mask, document size);
- cases: `image.crop`; a filter (e.g. Gaussian Blur with a radius param); selections (ellipse, add/subtract, feather, inverse, then fill); `type.create` with size/colour/font params (text content and style survive, rendered pixels match);
- at 8/16/32-bit where the command supports it; one undo step per played step.
If a case exposes a real replay bug, it is reported in its own issue rather than fixed here.

title: New Document: split Mobile into iOS and Android, add current Android devices and a Billboard category
author: snipeTR
body:
## Summary

File › New has a single **Mobile** category that mixes Apple devices with one generic Android size (`Android 1080p`, 1080 x 1920). There are also no presets for large-format outdoor print (billboards), which are a common File › New starting point.

Proposal (all in `crates/ui-egui/src/new_doc_ui.rs` `CATEGORIES`):

1. **Split Mobile into two categories, iOS and Android**, in the place Mobile has now (after Web).
2. **Keep names short and readable** on both sides (cards are 164 pt wide).
3. **Add current, popular Android device presets** (Samsung, Google, Huawei foldables).
4. **Add a Billboard category** for large-format print, at the real printed size and a large-format resolution.
5. **Keep the existing structure**: the `Preset` type `(name, width px, height px, ppi)`, `apply_preset`, and 72 ppi for screen presets stay as they are.

## Proposed presets

**Mobile (iOS)**: 72 ppi

| iPhone 16-17-18 Pro | 1206 x 2622 |
| iPhone 16-17-18 Pro Max | 1320 x 2868 |
| iPad Pro 13" | 2064 x 2752 |

**Mobile (Android)**: 72 ppi

| Preset | Pixels |
|---|---|

title: Format: ZIP entry lookup is linear per tile and CRC-32 is byte-at-a-time
author: vangel76
body:
`crates/format/src/zip.rs`:

1. `ZipReader::find` scans `entries` linearly by name. Loading a `.pcraft` bundle calls it once per tile reference (via `ZipSource::get` → `read_by_name`), so a load is O(refs × entries) string compares: for a bundle with ~50k tile objects that is on the order of 10^9 comparisons. `photocraft-io`'s OpenRaster reader (`ora.rs`) uses the same lookup per layer.
2. `crc32` is a hand-rolled byte-at-a-time table CRC-32, run over every entry on save and on load. `crc32fast` (already in `Cargo.lock` through `flate2`) computes the same IEEE CRC with slicing-by-16 / SIMD.

Fix: build a name → index map once in `ZipReader::new` (keeping the current first-match behaviour for duplicate names) and use it in `find`; implement `crc32` with `crc32fast`.

title: Format: a .pcraft pattern's declared size isn't checked on load (a tiny file can abort the app)
author: vangel76
body:
A `.pcraft` pattern stores its `width`/`height` in the manifest and its pixels as tiles. On load (`crates/format/src/convert.rs`, the `patterns` loop in `document()`), the declared size is copied as-is. A pattern can claim 65535 × 65535 px and have no tiles at all, so the file stays about 1 KB.

When anything paints that pattern (a Pattern Fill layer, Pattern Overlay, a pattern stroke):
- `photocraft_compose::pattern::pattern_rgba` allocates `width × height × 16` bytes (64 GiB here). That's an allocation failure, which aborts the process and can't be caught. `PreparedPatterns::get` also falls back to an unbudgeted `Tile::new_in` when the budget refuses the pattern.
- `crates/engine/src/pattern_cmds.rs` (`brush_texture`, `average_color`) computes `(width * height) as usize` in `u32`. That panics in debug builds and wraps in release.
- The GPU plan only filters out empty patterns before uploading one as a texture.

So opening a tiny hostile file aborts the app.

Expected: the loader rejects a pattern that's 0 px on a side or larger than the PSD reader's 30 000 px edge limit (`Corrupt`/`LimitExceeded`). Renderers and commands refuse a pattern too large to paint instead of allocating for it, and use overflow-free size math.

body:
On NVIDIA, a single start that is killed before its first frame switches PhotoCraft to CPU rendering, with
llvmpipe drawing the window, even though Vulkan works fine. If the "Switched to CPU rendering" dialog isn't
answered, every later launch stays on software rendering without saying why.

This is one way a config ends up in the state behind #1461. Since #2206 (0.7.0) that state no longer fails with
`no graphics adapter found`; it now starts quietly on llvmpipe instead.

**Setup:** PhotoCraft 0.7.0 (official x86_64 tarball) and `main` @ `953390a`. RTX 5070, NVIDIA 615.71.09,
Mesa 26.2.4, Fedora 44 (distrobox), on headless sway (wlroots), **not KWin or GNOME**. Each run used a fresh,
throwaway `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.

**Repro:**

1. Start PhotoCraft and `kill -9` it as soon as `gpu-starting.json` appears. The marker reads
   `{"adapter":"","adapterBackend":"","backend":"auto",…}`, so no adapter had been chosen yet.
2. Start it again. The log has
   `Plan { backend: Gl, reason: Some("the previous start didn't finish on auto; using gl"), remember: true }`,
   then `gl not compatible with provided surface`. It relaunches with `--safe-gpu` on llvmpipe and shows
   "Switched to CPU rendering". `preferences.json` already says `"renderingMode": "cpu", "useGpu": false`,
   although neither button has been pressed.
3. Quit without answering the dialog (I killed it) and start a third time: `Plan { backend: Cpu, reason: None }`,
   llvmpipe, and no dialog. With a clean config the same machine starts on `Auto` with the Vulkan RTX 5070.

window (the limitation #1337 hit), so the GL step always fails and the chain is really Vulkan → CPU.
`remember_cpu` in `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs` then saves CPU mode from `on_started` as soon as the relaunch

title: Format: harden blob/zip reads against size overflow and foreign entries
author: vangel76
body:
There are two panic paths in `photocraft-format`'s bundle readers:

1. **Blob size overflow** (`crates/format/src/store.rs`, `LoadFetch::blob`): `take(self.opts.max_blob_bytes as u64 + 1)` overflows when a caller passes `LoadOptions { max_blob_bytes: usize::MAX, .. }`, which means "unlimited". In debug builds that's a panic. In release builds it wraps to `take(0)`, so every blob decodes to 0 bytes and fails its hash check, and no bundle with blobs (ICC profile, PSD raw blocks, …) loads. `ZipReader::read` already handles this with `saturating_add` (see its `deflated_entry_with_unbounded_limit_round_trips` test).
2. **Unchecked ZIP slice** (`crates/format/src/zip.rs`, `ZipReader::read`): `&self.bytes[e.data_offset..e.data_offset + e.compressed]` is unchecked, but `Entry` is `pub` and `Clone`. Reading an entry from another archive (or a larger one) through a reader panics instead of returning an error.

While there, the bounded zstd decode in `blob()` duplicates `decompress()`, the big-endian branch in `Collect::tile` duplicates `tile_le()`, and `existing_object_is_valid` computes the expected bytes twice (once for the length, once in `matches_content_hash`).

Expected: both paths return `Err`. The duplicates can share one helper.

title: Autosave: a committed save can report failure, and orphaned recovery data is never cleaned
author: vangel76
body:
Two problems in `crates/format` around directory saves and autosave recovery:

1. **A committed save can report failure.** `PcraftWriter::save_dir` (`store.rs`) writes the manifest (the commit point) and then deletes objects the new manifest no longer references with `std::fs::remove_file(..)?`. If one of those deletions fails (the file vanished, it is locked on Windows, or a stray non-file sits at that path), the whole save returns `Err` although the document was saved completely. For autosave that turns a successful save into a reported failure.
2. **Orphaned recovery data is never cleaned.** `autosave.rs` writes the bundle first and the `<key>.json` sidecar afterwards. `list_recovery` skips bundles without a sidecar, and nothing ever deletes them, so a crash during a document's first autosave leaves a partial `<key>.pcraft` folder in the recovery directory forever. Likewise, `*.pcsave.tmp` files that `atomic.rs` leaves behind after a crash are never swept (`list_objects` only looks at `.zst`).

Fix: make the post-commit cleanup best-effort; when the app opens its recovery store, sweep sidecar-less bundles and stale temp files that belong to another process and have not been touched for a while (so another running instance's in-progress save is never touched). Bundles with a sidecar are never removed.

title: Type: triple-click selects a line, quadruple a paragraph, five clicks all text (TYPE-218-8)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #218 (scorecard TYPE-218-8, docs/gaps.md G8).

## What's missing on main
While editing type on the canvas, a double-click selects the word under the caret (`canvas.rs` → `type_tool::select_word`). Triple-, quadruple- and quintuple-clicks do nothing more, and there are no tests for the multi-click selections.

## Photoshop's behaviour
With the Type tool in a text layer: double-click selects a word, triple-click selects the line, quadruple-click selects the paragraph, and five clicks select all of the text in the layer.
Sources: [Julieanne Kost (Adobe), 30 tips for working with type in Photoshop](https://jkost.com/blog/2020/09/30-tips-tricks-and-shortcuts-for-working-with-type-in-photoshop.html); Adobe's text shortcut table lists double/triple/quadruple-click for word/line/paragraph ([helpx](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop-elements/using/keys-using-text.html)).

## Proposal
- Count consecutive clicks at the same spot (within the system double-click time and distance) in the type tool; 2 → word, 3 → visual line (as laid out, for point and paragraph type, horizontal and vertical), 4 → paragraph (up to the hard return), 5 → all text.
- Keep it agent-drivable: the selection helpers work on the `text_edit` state (and existing `type.navigate`/selection paths where they apply), so tests can drive them without real clicks.
- Tests: each click count selects the expected range in multi-line paragraph text and multi-paragraph point text; a 6th click / clicks far apart restart at a caret; an empty layer and out-of-range carets don't panic.
- Flip TYPE-218-8 in `scorecard/type.toml`, regenerate `docs/scorecard.md`, update G8.

title: Automation: xtask check that every panel button routes through a command id (AUTO-219-8)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #219 (scorecard AUTO-219-8).

## What's missing on main
AGENTS.md rule 1: every user-visible action is a command, and the UI is thin: panels must dispatch engine commands (or shell `UI_COMMANDS`) by id so the UI, CLI, control channel and MCP stay equivalent. Nothing checks this: a panel button can still mutate the document directly and stay invisible to agents, actions and history. The scorecard row reads "No such xtask check".

## Proposal
- `cargo xtask` gets a check (a new subcommand, run from `xtask ci`) that scans `crates/ui-egui/src` for button-like widgets in panel code and fails when a click handler mutates the session/document directly instead of going through a command id (`app.run(...)`, `menus::invoke(...)`, or a known shell UI command).
- Existing exceptions go into an explicit, commented allowlist (file + reason), so the check is green on day one and the list can only shrink; the check reports new violations with file:line.
- Tests: the scanner's unit tests over small fixtures (a routed button passes, a direct mutation fails, an allowlisted one passes, a stale allowlist entry is reported).
- Document it in `docs/development.md`, flip AUTO-219-8 in `scorecard/automation.toml` (partial if the allowlist is non-empty), regenerate `docs/scorecard.md`.

No Photoshop behaviour involved; this is infrastructure for agent parity.

title: PSD export: a type layer created by family name is written with an invented font name ("<Family>-Regular"), so Photoshop treats the font as missing and replaces it on edit
author: adammthayer-sketch
body:
## Summary

On 0.7.0, `type.create` with a font given by family name writes a font name into the type layer's EngineData that no installed font has: the family name with its spaces removed, plus `-Regular`. Photoshop looks fonts up by their real PostScript name, so it shows the font as missing and substitutes Myriad Pro as soon as the text is edited, even though the font is installed and PhotoCraft rendered with it.

| `font` passed to `type.create` | `/FontSet … /Name` written to the PSD | Real PostScript name |
|---|---|---|
| `Haettenschweiler` | `Haettenschweiler-Regular` | `Haettenschweiler` |
| `Franklin Gothic Demi Cond` | `FranklinGothicDemiCond-Regular` | `FranklinGothic-DemiCond` |

title: Contributors: a way to claim an issue so PRs don't collide
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
With this many contributors, several people often fix the same issue at once. Counting PRs that say they fix an issue (`Fixes #N` or `(#N)` in the title): **108 issues have fixing PRs from two or more authors, and 87 of those PRs were closed unmerged**. 72 of those collisions started since Oct 8. Some are open right now, for example #3469 (three open PRs) and #3497, #3514, #3391, #3368, #3365 (two each).

Today a claim is whatever comes first: a comment, an empty draft PR, or a finished PR. People find out about each other only after the work is done, and reviewers have to compare competing PRs.

Some options, roughly from least to most effort:

1. **Say how to claim, in `docs/contributing.md` and the PR template.** For example: comment on the issue before starting, and search open PRs for `#N` first. Also say whether an empty draft PR counts as a claim, and how long a claim lasts without code (24 hours, say).
2. **Assign the issue to whoever claims it.** GitHub lets maintainers assign anyone who has commented on the issue, so the claim shows in the issue list, and `no:assignee` lists what's free. A small workflow could do this on a `/take` comment and drop stale assignments.
3. **Flag collisions automatically.** A workflow that comments on a new PR when another open PR already fixes the same issue, so the second author finds out at once rather than at review.

Happy to help with any of these if one sounds right.

title: Face-Aware Liquify
author: manoiese
body:
# Feature Request: Face-Aware Liquify Tool

## Summary

I would love to see a Face-Aware Liquify tool in PhotoCraft, similar to the feature available in Adobe Photoshop.

This is one of the features I use most in Photoshop, and having it in PhotoCraft would be a major improvement to my photo editing workflow.

## Proposed Features

- **Automatic face detection:** Automatically detect faces and identify facial features such as the eyes, eyebrows, nose, mouth, jawline, and overall face shape.
- **Interactive facial landmarks:** Display draggable control points directly on the detected facial features, allowing users to reshape them intuitively with the mouse.
- **Facial adjustments:** Easily adjust eye size and position, nose width, mouth size, lip shape, face width, jawline, and chin.
- **Real-time preview:** Show the results immediately while dragging control points or adjusting sliders.
- **Multiple faces:** Allow users to select and edit individual faces when a photograph contains multiple people.
- **Non-destructive editing:** Preserve the original image and allow adjustments to be modified or reverted.
- **GPU acceleration:** Use GPU acceleration where available for smooth, responsive editing.

## User Experience

The ideal workflow would be to open a portrait, select the Face-Aware Liquify tool, and have PhotoCraft automatically detect the face and display interactive control points.

Users could then click and drag the points to reshape facial features, or use sliders for more precise adjustments, without manually warping the entire image.

## Motivation

I frequently use Photoshop's Face-Aware Liquify feature for portrait retouching. It makes facial adjustments incredibly fast and intuitive compared to traditional manual liquify tools.

I believe this feature would be a valuable addition to PhotoCraft, especially for photographers who want professional portrait-retouching capabilities in an open-source application.

Thank you for your work on PhotoCraft!

title: Responsive artboards: extend solver geometry and metadata robustness
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## Context
The responsive-artboard implementation supplies a deterministic rule solver and bounded diagnostics, but its first delivery intentionally excludes some geometric and malformed-input cases.

## Follow-up
- Add property tests for idempotence, A→B→A stability, clamp adherence, monotonicity, and native/WASM determinism.
- Extend geometry coverage for rotated layers, masks/clipping, nested and empty groups, background layers, cross-artboard layers, zero/extreme aspect ratios, and text smaller than its minimum-size constraints.
- Specify safe visual bounds for layer effects (or retain the documented exclusion with explicit diagnostic behavior).
- Fuzz versioned native metadata and `.responsive.json` parsing, including size limits and graceful degradation.

## Acceptance
No input causes a panic or silent document corruption; solver invariants hold across generated valid inputs; documented unsupported geometry produces explicit, stable results.

This is follow-up work after the initial responsive-artboard delivery; it is not required to review its existing implementation.

title: Responsive artboards: benchmark large variant sets and cache memory
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## Context
The responsive-artboard UI caches previews by document revision and bounds diagnostic work, but there is no dedicated benchmark for large variant sets or cache memory behavior.

## Follow-up
- Add a reproducible release benchmark for a large document with 500 layers × 10 variants (plus smaller/larger comparison points).
- Measure overview refresh, variant switch, diagnostic recomputation, preview latency, and memory while scrolling/refreshing.
- Add sweeps for 100/500/1000 layers × 4/10 variants and verify cache invalidation and an explicit memory cap/eviction policy.
- Improve semantic collision checks beyond bounding-box overlap where practical, while retaining bounded work and explicit truncation.

## Initial same-device check
On 2026-10-11, the existing 4,000×3,000 / 174-layer UI harness was run on Windows (AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 / Radeon 860M) against upstream and the responsive branch, three repetitions each. Idle-frame medians were 1.04 ms upstream and 1.48 ms on the branch; interaction measurements had large GPU-related outliers (roughly 700–800 ms) on both runs. This harness contains no responsive variants, so the small sample is noisy and does not establish the overview's large-document performance.

## Acceptance
The new benchmark is reproducible on the same machine, records medians and tail latency plus memory, and demonstrates the 500×10 scenario stays within an agreed refresh budget without unbounded cache growth.

title: Responsive artboards: add interactive propagation conflict resolution
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## Context
Master propagation currently preserves variant-only subtrees and reports removed master mappings, retained content, and stale overrides. The result is safe and reviewable, but remediation is still a command-level workflow.

## Follow-up
Design a focused conflict review flow that lets people inspect each affected variant and choose how to resolve preserved local layers and stale overrides (keep, remap, or remove where valid). Include deleted/renamed master layers, undo/redo as one intentional operation, and clear handling when the source layer no longer exists. The all-artboards overview already provides side-by-side comparison; improve it only where it directly supports conflict resolution.

## Acceptance
Every conflict is visible with its affected variant/layer and available actions; no content is discarded without an explicit choice; resolution is undoable and covered by engine/UI tests.

title: Responsive artboards: accessibility and workflow-state audit
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## Context
The responsive workflow has keyboard navigation, localized labels, background progress for expensive reflow, and explicit error handling. A full accessibility and empty/error-state review has not been completed.

## Follow-up
- Audit keyboard-only navigation and focus order across overview, findings, role/rule editors, variant switching, and export preflight.
- Check accessible names and announcements for screen readers, warning presentation for color-vision differences, and scaling at high UI zoom.
- Review RTL behavior and tablet/pen interaction for canvas overlays and selection.
- Add explicit empty, failed-reflow, stale-cache, and long-running progress states where the review finds gaps.

## Acceptance
Document the tested matrix and fix actionable issues with egui UI tests or a concise manual verification record.

title: Responsive artboards: verify PSD metadata and export interoperability
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## Context
`.pcraft` versioned responsive metadata and the versioned PSD semantic-role annotation have automated structural tests. Interoperability behavior after other editors resave the PSD has not been observed in those applications.

## Follow-up
- Verify the PhotoCraft `shmd` role annotation against the public PSD specification and add size-bounded, real-file round-trip/fuzz coverage.
- Test open/save/resave in Photoshop, Photopea, GIMP, and Affinity where available; record whether the block is preserved, ignored, or removed and whether unknown PSD blocks remain intact.
- Verify the current single-artboard PDF/SVG and web behavior, then document any required platform-specific limits. Keep multi-variant export semantics explicit.

## Acceptance
Publish an evidence-based compatibility/degradation matrix with application versions and sample files; no unsupported editor-preservation claim is made without a direct check.

title: PS v1-v19 Feature Request: Snap-to-guidelines grid intersection support for Distort / Corner-pin transformations
author: b72i
body:
Hi PhotoCrast Team,

I would like to request a feature regarding guide snapping during perspective/distort transformations (corner pinning), modeled after Photoshop’s legacy behavior prior to version 20 (CC 2019).

**Requested Feature**
When performing a Distort / Corner Pin transformation on an image or layer, individual corner handles should magnetically snap precisely to guide lines and guide line intersections.

**Background & How Photoshop Handled This**

Pre-v20 (v19 and earlier):
Photoshop’s legacy transformation engine calculated bounding box corner points individually against the snap-grid matrix. When dragging a single corner handle in Distort mode (Ctrl/Cmd + Drag), the corner point easily snapped to guide intersections, making it effortless to align images to exact perspective grids or templates.

Changes in Photoshop v20 (CC 2019) & Why It Stopped Working:
In CC 2019 (v20), Adobe overhauled the Free Transform engine to unify behavior across Creative Cloud apps and vector tools.
They introduced dynamic vector-mesh transformation matrices under the hood instead of direct absolute pixel/corner coordinates during free distortion.
The Ctrl/Cmd modifier key—which activates free corner dragging—was hardcoded to override/bypass snap constraints in the new engine logic.
As a result, guide snapping during perspective distortion was completely lost (unless users manually reverted to the "Legacy Free Transform" mode in preferences).

**Why This Feature is Crucial for PhotoCrast**
In graphic design, mockups, and architectural/perspective layout workflows, snapping distorted image corners to guide intersections is vital for speed and accuracy. Implementing this legacy-style snap behavior would give PhotoCrast a major workflow advantage for power users who rely heavily on precise guide alignment.

Thank you for considering this addition to the roadmap!

title: PSD: path subpaths() reserves up to 229 KB per length record, aborts on hostile vmsk (1.1)
author: vangel76
body: `PathData::subpaths()` (crates/psd/src/path.rs) calls `Vec::with_capacity(remaining.min(4096))` for every length record, where `remaining` is a u16 from the file. PsdKnot is 56 bytes, so each record reserves ~229 KB; `from_bytes` accepts up to 4,000,000 records, so a ~2 MB vmsk/vsms block of consecutive length records (count 0xFFFF) reserves ~15 GB and `with_capacity` aborts instead of returning an error. Fix: don't preallocate.

title: PSD: descriptor lists preallocate n items from the file, 10-20x amplification (1.2)
author: vangel76
body: In crates/psd/src/descriptor.rs, `Vec::with_capacity(n)` for descriptor items, reference items and VlLs lists uses n from the file. `check_count` only demands 10/8/4 bytes per item while items cost ~100/~80 bytes, so a large tdta/lfx2/SoLd block reserves 10-20x its size up front, and `with_capacity` aborts rather than erroring. Fix: cap the preallocation (vectors still grow as items parse).

title: Crop tool: a resized crop frame stops short of the snap line when the handle isn't grabbed exactly (recrop leaves a transparent strip)
author: davidmann4
body:
Split out of #1919 (reported there by @theriseandfallofitall).

### Steps
1. Open an image, pick the Crop tool, turn **Delete Cropped Pixels** off, crop to an inner rectangle and commit. The pixels outside stay on the layer, hidden.
2. Pick Crop again with View › Snap on and drag an edge or corner handle outward toward the hidden image edge until the snap line shows. Commit.

### Actual
The snap line sits on the hidden image edge, but the frame stops a few pixels short of it or past it. Committing leaves a transparent strip along that side, or cuts off a few pixels.

### Expected
The frame edge lands exactly on the edge the snap line shows, as in Photoshop. No transparent strip.

### Cause
In `crates/ui-egui/src/snap_ui.rs`, `live_crop_handle` snapped the handle only for default-mode resizes with **Auto Center Preview** on. Every other resize (Auto Center off, or Classic Mode) fell back to snapping the **pointer**. A handle can be grabbed up to the grab radius (8 screen px) away from it, so the frame missed the target by exactly that grab offset. Grabbing exactly on the handle snaps correctly, which is why a quick check can look fine. The snap targets themselves are right: the hidden edge's `LayerEdge` wins on every axis, and no other layer edge or centre beats it.

Reproduced on main @ 308ef632 with a harness test: 24 of 32 combinations fail (Classic Mode × Auto Center × right/top edge, top-left/bottom-right corner × grab offset ±4 px).

title: PSD: composite_rgba8 skips the output budget and converts planes with infallible allocation (1.3)
author: vangel76
body:
`PsdFile::composite_rgba8` decodes the merged image and converts each plane (`plane_to_u8`, `unpack_bits`) before any check on the RGBA output size, unlike `Layer::rgba8`. `unpack_bits`/`plane_to_u8` allocate infallibly (abort instead of Err) and multiply width*height unchecked. A large 1-bit/16-bit PSB can allocate GBs with no recovery.

Fix: apply the `n*4 <= MAX_DECODED_BYTES` guard first and use fallible allocation in the plane conversions.

title: PSD: a tiny pattern with a huge rectangle zero-pads up to 8 GiB (1.4)
author: vangel76
body:
In `crates/psd/src/patterns.rs`, a pattern channel whose rectangle is much smaller than the pattern rectangle passes the input-size check (only the small channel size is compared with the data) and is zero-padded to the full pattern plane. The only cap is `MAX_DECODED_BYTES` (8 GiB) summed over up to 66 channels, so a few-hundred-byte pattern declaring 30000x30000 with 1x1 channels allocates gigabytes of zeros.

Fix: a named total budget for zero-padded channel planes. Real files write channel rects equal to the pattern rect and are unaffected.

Add a built-in procedural scatter primitive (e.g. `filter.render.scatter {count, size range, opacity range, distribution}`) constrained to the layer/selection, for stochastic texture generation.

## Motivation

Hand-rolled scatter loops (e.g. rain rings on water) took three audit rounds before texture stopped reading as a lattice. An in-engine scatter filter would produce better randomness than a driver-side RNG loop, and would be drivable by agents like every other command.

## Diagnosis

No in-engine stochastic texture primitive exists today (the Render menu has Clouds, Difference Clouds, Fibers, Lens Flare, Lighting Effects, Relight — nothing that scatters shapes/dabs isotropically; Scattering only exists as a brush-dynamics section).

## Details

Driver-side isotropic clustered scatter with wind drift + size growth toward bottom.

## Evidence

- serene-lake-view-in-ngawa-tibetan-prefecture-rebuild/pass6_fixes.py
- serene-lake-view-in-ngawa-tibetan-prefecture-rebuild/pass7_fixes.py

title: paint.stroke fill mode (closed outlines render as rings)
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
### Summary

`paint.stroke` paints dabs along the path only. When an agent (or user) drives a closed-outline gesture intended as an organic filled dab — e.g. a blob or patch of paint — the result renders as a **ring**: paint lands on the outline, the interior stays untouched. There is no `fill` mode on `paint.stroke` and no fill-oriented primitive to reach for.

### What happened

Strokes paint along the path only, so a closed-outline gesture intended as a dab renders as a ring. This cost two audit-fix rounds in the serene-lake campaign (spiral-bullseye defects): the only workaround today is filling the interior with many overlapping interior strokes, never closed outlines.

### Diagnosis

By-design stroke semantics; an organic-fill workflow gap for painting agents.

### Feature ask

One of:

- a `fill: true` option on `paint.stroke` that fills the region enclosed by a closed point list (soft BrushSettings edges), or
- a `paint.dab {x, y, r}` command that paints a single soft-edged dab with the session/`BrushSettings` brush.

Either removes this whole failure class for organic painting agents.

### Evidence

- serene-lake-view-in-ngawa-tibetan-prefecture-rebuild/audits/rebuild-v2-default.txt
- serene-lake-view-in-ngawa-tibetan-prefecture-rebuild/audits/rebuild-v3-default.txt

### Environment

- First seen: 2026-10-11 (serene-lake-view-in-ngawa-tibetan-prefecture-rebuild)
- Component: engine (`paint.stroke` in `crates/engine/src/brush_cmds.rs`, spec in `crates/engine/src/commands.rs`)

title: MCP server processes accumulate indefinitely (no idle exit, no singleton lock per root pair)
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## What happened

`pgrep` showed ~13 concurrent `photocraft-cli mcp` processes (from other sessions), each pinning `--automation-read-root`/`--automation-write-root` indefinitely. No failure occurs, but this is a resource/ownership hazard on a shared machine.

## Diagnosis

Ops smell: there is no reaper for dead-session servers.

- `photocraft-cli mcp` runs the MCP server over stdio until the client disconnects (`crates/automation/src/server/transport.rs` — reader exits on stdin EOF, then `serve_io` tears down). A client that exits cleanly reaps its server, but any orphaned or non-exiting client leaves the process alive forever.
- There is no idle-exit timer and no singleton/lock per root pair anywhere in `crates/automation` (`workspace.rs` only opens the roots; no flock/pid file).

## Proposed direction

Either of:

- idle exit after N minutes without a request, or
- a singleton lock per read/write root pair (second instance for the same pair fails or attaches).

## Workaround

None; harmless until ports/memory pressure.

## Evidence

- First seen 2026-10-11 in `reflection-of-trees-on-a-calm-lake-rebuild` (`docs/mcp-cli-issues.md` there).

title: Unattended app death with no breadcrumb: optional --heartbeat-file so supervisors can distinguish dead from wedged
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
### What happened

A control-instance app (pid recorded) was found dead at a phase start (connection refused, process gone); cause never determined — no OOM line checked at the time and the launcher's app.log was overwritten by the relaunch redirect.

### Diagnosis

suspected-unverified — cause not determined.

### Notes from triage (2026-10-11)

The app already has a rotating on-disk log (`logs/photocraft.log` → `photocraft.1.log` → `photocraft.2.log`, PR #1143, `apps/photocraft/src/logging.rs`), so a crashed run's log survives the next launch — but an external launcher redirecting its own app.log still overwrites it, and nothing in the app distinguishes a dead process from a wedged one. An external kill (supervisor deadline, OOM) leaves no record by construction.

### Proposed

An optional `--heartbeat-file <path>` (or equivalent): the app touches the file periodically while its event loop runs, so a supervisor can distinguish dead from wedged and check for an OOM/crash breadcrumb before relaunching.

### Workaround

none; recovery was relaunch + resume from corpus

title: 60s per-request timeout reply is ambiguous per op
author: ahmedhosnypro
body: The identical 'timeout: no reply in 60s — the command may still be running' reply had opposite outcomes: layer.new.layer never applied (safe to re-send) while paint.stroke did apply (re-send would double-apply). Proposed app fix: idempotency keys on engine.execute or a journal/last-op-status method keyed by request id.

title: Sample All Layers does not work when the active layer is fully transparent
author: jarallahassalami
body:
When using the Spot Healing / healing brush with **Sample All Layers** enabled, the tool fails to apply any edit if the currently active layer is fully transparent (empty). The edit is silently ignored, or no visible change is produced, even though the source pixels exist on other visible layers below.

This forces the user to either edit directly on the image layer or duplicate it first, which defeats the purpose of using "Sample All Layers" on a separate retouch layer — a standard non-destructive workflow.

**Steps to reproduce:**

- Open an image (single raster layer with content).
- Add a new empty (fully transparent) layer above it.
- Select the new transparent layer as the active layer.
- Enable **Sample All Layers** in the tool options.
- Choose the Spot Healing brush (or any healing/cloning tool that supports sampling).
- Try to remove an object / spot on the image.
- Observe: nothing is applied to the transparent layer, or the tool does not respond

**Expected behavior:**

With **Sample All Layers** enabled, the tool should sample pixels from the composite of all visible layers and apply the healed result onto the currently active (transparent) layer — the same way Photoshop and similar editors behave.

**Actual behavior:**

The edit is not applied. The transparent layer remains empty. No error is shown.

**Workaround:**
- Edit directly on the image layer (destructive), or
- Duplicate the image layer and edit on the copy.

**Why this matters:**
Non-destructive retouching on a separate layer is a core workflow. Without this, users must modify the original pixels, which is a significant regression in usability compared to other editors.

title: fix(automation): engine.commands reports enabled:false for every command with no document — no way to tell "no document" from "not runnable"
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
Filed from a recorded automation issue (first seen 2026-10-11).

## What happened

With no document open, `engine.commands` (the JSON-lines control method; also the MCP `command_list` tool) reports `enabled: false` for `paint.stroke`, every `layer.*`, every `filter.*` — yet these are exactly the commands an agent must plan around, and they all ran fine once a document existed. The registry gives no way to distinguish "no document open" from "not runnable".

## Why it matters

An agent reads `enabled` as a hard precondition, concludes the commands are unavailable, and mis-plans the session. Current workaround: ignore the `enabled` flag when planning and verify by running the command.

## Diagnosis

Enablement conflates document state with runnability. `Headless::command_list` emits only a boolean:

```rust
"enabled": self.session.is_enabled(c.id),
```

`Session::is_enabled` resolves to the command's `enabled` closure, which for document commands returns false whenever `session.active()` is `None`. The engine already computes a human-readable `Session::disabled_reason(id)` (crates/engine/src/lib.rs), but the command listing never exposes it, so a caller cannot tell which precondition failed.

## Suggested direction

Include `disabled_reason` (or a `reason: null | "no-document" | …` field) in the `engine.commands` / `command_list` output, so "no document" is distinguishable from a genuine precondition failure.

title: Secondary keyboard bindings: a command can hold only one shortcut, so Photoshop's F2/F3/F4 and the ⌘+/⌘= pairs can't be expressed
author: bitshiftza
body:
## Summary

A command can hold exactly **one** keyboard shortcut in PhotoCraft. Photoshop's default set gives

not by a user in Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts. The shape of the limit:

- `shortcuts::effective_shortcut` / `default_shortcut` mirror that in the shell — `crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs:76,81`

This came up in #2405 (closed) and #2366: F2 can't be the default for Rename Layer because F2 is
Photoshop's Edit › Cut, and Cut can't also answer F2 because it already holds ⌘X.

## What it costs us today

**1. The function-key block is half-implemented.** `crates/ui-egui/src/menu_catalog.rs` already
carries Photoshop's legacy keys:

| Key | Command | Line |
|---|---|---|
| F5 | `window.panel.brushSettings` | `:742` |
| F6 | `window.panel.color` | `:748` |
| F7 | `window.panel.layers` | `:755` |

`Cmd++` before `Cmd+=`"). A user…

title: document.pixel reply scale undocumented (floats 0..1)
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## What happened

`document.pixel` returns RGBA floats 0..1 (e.g. `[1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]` after a #ff00ff stroke), not 0..255; the docs table states the range for neither `document.pixel` nor `document.sampleColor`. A client assuming 0..255 mis-reads every probe.

## Diagnosis

docs gap

## Workaround / fix

multiply by 255 (or compare in float space) when probing

## Evidence

- /home/ahmed/Projects/artwork/june_3-rebuild/docs/photocraft-app-mcp-issues.md
- /home/ahmed/Projects/artwork/june_3-rebuild/docs/session-bug-contract.md

title: Control protocol: auth succeeds while the engine is wedged (false liveness signal) — add a health method reporting frame-loop liveness
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
During app wedges, `auth` replied in milliseconds while `ui.inspect`/`engine.execute` stalled — a liveness check built on auth gives false confidence and slows first diagnosis.

**Proposed:** a health control method reporting frame-loop liveness / last-frame age (e.g. seconds since the last frame, or whether the frame loop is currently blocked), so automation agents can distinguish a wedged frame loop from a healthy connection.

**Diagnosis:** `auth` is handled on the control-server socket thread before the frame loop (`authentication_reply` in `apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs`, via `crates/automation/src/security.rs`) — it is not a liveness probe.

**Workaround:** probe `ui.inspect` (or another frame-drained method) for liveness, never `auth`.

Companion: the frame-starvation wedge itself (display asleep / fully occluded on Wayland) is tracked in #2493.

title: fix(automation): a second auth on an authenticated connection returns a misleading unknown-method error
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## What happened

`auth` is valid only as the first frame of a TCP connection. A second `auth` call on the same (already authenticated) connection returns:

- headless `serve` TCP: `unknown method \`auth\` (try \`methods\`)` (`crates/automation/src/rpc.rs` dispatch fallthrough)
- desktop control server: `unknown method \`auth\`` (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` dispatch fallthrough)

The suggested `methods` fallback is itself misleading: as the first frame of a fresh connection, `methods` answers `authentication required` (`crates/automation/src/security.rs` `authentication_reply`). So an agent that follows the error's advice hits a second confusing error.

## Expected

Auth-once per connection is reasonable. The error for a repeat `auth` should say the connection is already authenticated, e.g. `already authenticated`, instead of routing into the unknown-method fallthrough.

## Workaround

Call `auth` exactly once per connection.

## Evidence

- Observed 2026-10-11 (pipeline validation step) while driving `serve` over TCP: a second `auth` on the same socket returned `unknown method \`auth\` (try \`methods\`)` even though the first auth had succeeded.

title: CLI: run-this-command-file mode for scripted builds
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
### Type
Feature request (component: CLI)

### What happened
Multi-step scripted builds currently require a hand-written Python TCP driver.

### Proposal
Add a "run this command file" mode to `photocraft-cli`, e.g.:

```
photocraft-cli run --control PORT --token-file F script.jsonl
```

Each line of the file is `{"command":…,"params":…}`, with a small template syntax for captured ids (e.g. `"layer": "$snags"`).

### Context
- Diagnosis: ergonomics gap; the stopgap (a scripted TCP driver) is proven to work.
- Feature ask: the scripted-TCP driver pattern, generalized into the CLI so scripted builds don't need hand-written drivers.

title: Displace smart filter ignores its mapPath: re-render drops the map
author: horknfbr
body:
## What happens

A Displace filter applied to a smart object does nothing. `filter.distort.displace` with a `mapPath` is recorded as a smart filter, but the rendered pixels are identical to the unfiltered layer. That holds when the filter is added and on every later re-render: Replace Contents, toggling the filter, transforming the layer.

## Steps

1. Make a document with a painted layer and convert it to a smart object (`layer.smartObjects.convertToSmartObject`).
2. Write a displacement map that is not mid-grey, e.g. solid white, to a PNG.
3. Run `filter.distort.displace` on the smart object with `{"horizontal":10,"vertical":10,"fit":"stretch","undefinedAreas":"repeat","mapPath":"<map.png>"}`.
4. Compare the composite with and without the filter.

**Expected:** pixels shift by up to `DISPLACE_PX × 10%`.
**Actual:** no change. We measured RMSE 0 between the flat and displaced renders.

## Why

Smart filters are rendered by `apply_smart_filters` → `filters::apply_filter_to_surface`, which builds `FilterParams` with `params_for` alone. That leaves `FilterParams::Displace { map: None, .. }`, and `distort2::displace` returns the source unchanged when there is no map. Only `run_filter` resolves `mapPath` (through `filters_ext::resolve`, which needs the session). It records just the params, then re-renders through the smart-filter path, so the resolved map is lost even on the first render.

## Notes

- A Displace smart filter that uses `mapDocument` has the same problem. Resolving it needs the session, so it would need the map stored with the filter, which is a separate change.
- On re-render this reads whatever path is stored in the filter params, including paths that come from a saved `.pcraft`. The direct command already does this, and `automation/src/workspace.rs` restricts `mapPath` only for agent commands.

title: PSD smart objects with a custom warp re-render stretched: Trnf frames the warp's control points, not the source rect
author: horknfbr
body:
## What happens

A PSD smart object with a custom warp is re-rendered stretched once its warp mesh's control points lie outside the source rectangle. "Re-rendered" here means Replace Contents, Edit Contents, a smart filter or a transform. The cached composite PhotoCraft shows on open is correct; the re-render is not.

## Why

`blocks::parse_smart` builds the smart object's affine by mapping the source rect `0..w × 0..h` (from `Sz`) onto the `Trnf` quad. For a `warpCustom` placement, Photoshop's `Trnf` is the image of the **bounding box of the 16 custom-warp control points**, which can extend past the source. Mapping the source rect counts the overhang twice. Export has the matching problem: `smart_map::quad_points` writes `Trnf` as the image of the source rect, so saving such a file shifts its quad.

## Measured

We measured this on a commercial shirt mockup with a 4200 × 4800 design smart object, whose mesh spills to x = −9 and y = −88. We replaced the contents and compared against Photoshop's own render of the same replacement:
- **`main`:** about a 1.6% vertical stretch, with the offset growing from 0 to −16 px top to bottom.
- **Control-point bounding box as the frame:** alignment exact everywhere, RMSE 0.49%.
- **Bounding box of the evaluated warp outline instead:** fixed that file but gave 5.4% RMSE on another, so the rule is specifically the control points.

The files are licensed, so they can't be attached. A synthetic `SoLd` whose mesh spills past `Sz` reproduces it.

## Not covered

The Distort/Perspective path (`parse_smart_perspective`, #426) still maps the source rect onto `nonAffineTransform` when a warp is also present. We have no Photoshop reference for that combination.

title: Mesh warps alias thin lines when shrinking: no minification filter, unlike the affine path
author: horknfbr
body:
## What happens

When a mesh warp shrinks its source a lot, thin lines alias: they come out crinkled, doubled or broken where Photoshop's render is smooth. This shows on any smart object placed through a warp, for example a 4200 × 4800 design placed at about 1/3–1/4 size on a shirt mockup. Edit › Transform › Warp, Puppet Warp and the Lens/Wide Angle corrections go through the same function.

## Why

`algo::warp::warp_triangles` takes one Catmull-Rom sample per output pixel and has no minification filter. The affine path, `transform::warp_surface`, already pre-reduces below 50% ("bicubic alone aliases below ~50%"); the mesh path has nothing equivalent.

## Measured

We compared against Photoshop's renders of the same Replace Contents on two commercial shirt mockups, using a design of 1 px grid lines:
- **White shirt:** RMSE 1.78% on `main`, 0.81% with per-pixel footprint filtering.
- **Pepper shirt:** 0.49% on `main`, 0.29% with the filtering.
- **A mockup without a warp:** unchanged.

The difference is entirely in thin-line sharpness; position and colour already match.

## Repro without the files

Place a source of 1 px lines every 4 px at 1/5 size through any non-identity mesh warp (e.g. Arc). The output has solid black pixels where the area average is 9/16 grey.

title: PSD: Displace smart filters (Dspl) aren't imported; mockups render flat
author: horknfbr
body:
## What happens

Photoshop **Displace** smart filters (Fltr class `Dspl`, filterID 1148416108) are not imported from PSD. They aren't in `smart_map`'s modelled filter list, so they become `psd.unsupportedFilter` and pass through on re-render. Mockup PSDs that bend a replaceable design over fabric depend on this filter. The usual stack is a design smart object, instanced 1–5 times, each instance with Displace → Gaussian Blur. Once the design is replaced, these render flat instead of following the folds.

## What Photoshop stores

Observed in real files:
- **The map is embedded in the filter descriptor,** under `DspD` (raw data, `tdta`):
  - a header of u32 LE height, u32 LE width and u16 LE mode (3)
  - then two 8-bit planes, horizontal then vertical, each width × height
  - then padding
- **Other keys:**
  - `HrzS`/`VrtS`: scale %
  - `DspM`: `StrF` stretch or `Tile`
  - `UndA`: `RptE` or `WrpA`
  - `EmbF`
  - `DspF`: an alias to the author's map file, usually unavailable
- **Map size:** in the files seen, the map has the document's size.

When it is stretched over the **document canvas** (not the layer bounds), PhotoCraft's existing `filter.distort.displace` reproduces Photoshop's render to within 1–2 levels, with exact alignment.

The files are licensed, so they can't be attached. The layout above is enough to build a synthetic fixture. The corpus has no `Dspl` file.

title: control: unknown-command errors give no near-match hint (e.g. engine.execute {"command": "engine.commands"})
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
Component: control-protocol

**What happened**

`engine.execute {"command": "engine.commands"}` fails with:

```
unknown command `engine.commands`
```

The command registry is only reachable as the top-level `engine.commands` protocol method; the in-engine equivalent is `command.list`. That mapping is already documented (docs/control-protocol.md: "`engine.commands` (or the engine command `command.list`) lists them all"), so the naming trap itself is intended. But the error gives no near-match hint, so an agent that guesses a command id has nothing to correct from and must re-list the whole registry.

**Suggested**

When `engine.execute` (and the control/serve/MCP dispatch) receives an unknown command id, include the nearest registered ids in the error (prefix or edit-distance match), e.g. `unknown command `engine.commands` — did you mean `command.list`?`

**Code**

- Error text: `EngineError::UnknownCommand` / `Session::disabled_reason_with` in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs` ("unknown command `{id}`").
- Top-level mapping: `"engine.commands" => app.run("command.list", …)` in `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`; same mapping in `crates/automation/src/rpc.rs` (headless serve).
- In-engine listing command: `command.list` in `crates/engine/src/commands.rs`.

First seen 2026-10-11 while driving the app over the control protocol from an agent session.

title: No history.undo command id (undo is edit.undo)
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
Recorded from an automation session (component: control-protocol).

## What happened

Undo exists as `edit.undo`; a `history.*` namespace exists (`history.deleteState`, `history.newDocument`) but not the most obvious member. Agents guessing `history.undo` get a hard error.

## Diagnosis

command naming inconsistency

## Workaround / fix

use `edit.undo`; proposed: alias `history.undo`

## Evidence

- Failed MCP calls recorded 2026-10-11 in an automation session (mcp-calls/failed/)
- Verified in the repo today: the engine registers only `history.deleteState` and `history.newDocument` under the `history.*` namespace (`crates/engine/src/history_cmds.rs`); there is no `history.undo`/`history.redo` alias, and unknown ids fail with `unknown command` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`).

Related: #2966 (History panel parity tracking, "Commands and MCP" section).

title: Automation/MCP: no server-side call log — tool attempts that fail at the transport layer (request never sent) leave no trace
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## What happened

Plan-phase `mcp__photocraft__session_list` failures (dead bridge, request never sent) were visible in the agent conversation but were not written to the session's call-logging corpus (`mcp-calls/failed/`). The logging law covers failed transports ("the request was not sent" counts as an attempt), but the harness-level MCP path had no logging hook, so the attempt escaped the corpus. The entry had to be logged retroactively, with an explanatory note that it is retroactive.

## Diagnosis

Logging-law gap at the MCP tool boundary: the call-logging corpus only sees calls that pass through the logging hook; an MCP tool attempt that fails at the transport layer (connection refused, connect timeout — the request never reaches the server) produces no log entry anywhere.

On the PhotoCraft side there is also no server-side record that would help reconstruct such attempts: the automation layer (`crates/automation`) — the rmcp MCP server (`server.rs`, `server/conventions.rs`), the bridge client (`bridge.rs`, which classifies `Failure::NotSent` vs `Failure::Transport` at lines ~107-113 and formats "the request was not sent" errors), the JSON-lines RPC server (`rpc.rs::serve_tcp`) and the desktop control server (`apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs`) — performs no request/audit logging at all (no `log::`/`tracing::` calls, no access log, no record of dropped connections). A failed attempt therefore appears only in the client's own error, never in any persisted log or corpus.

## Workaround / fix

Retroactive corpus entry, labeled as such.

## Requested behaviour

- MCP-tool attempts, **including transport failures** (request never sent), are corpus/audit entries.
- Retroactive entries must be labeled as retroactive.
- A server-side record of attempted calls and failures (e.g. an access/audit log or a `calls` log file the automation layer writes) would make the corpus reconstructable even when the client-side hook is missing.

## Evidence

- Harness-level: `/ho…

title: Orphaned daemons from dead sessions consume ports and linger
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
### What happened

At session start: a stale `photocraft-cli serve --port 7971` (its project has since been deleted) plus several `photocraft-cli mcp` servers from dead sessions, with nothing reaping them. One port was in the LISTEN state with no attributable process, forcing a fallback port to be chosen.

(MCP server processes accumulating indefinitely is tracked separately in #3660; this issue is about the `serve` TCP daemons and port ownership.)

### Diagnosis

No daemon lifecycle management across sessions:

- `photocraft-cli serve --port <port>` binds its loopback port and serves until killed: `photocraft_automation::rpc::serve_tcp` (`crates/automation/src/rpc.rs`) loops over `listener.incoming()` forever — no idle shutdown, no parent-death detection (`PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` or equivalent), no pid/lock file and no port-claim convention. Nothing reaps a daemon whose session died.
- If the fixed port is already taken, `TcpListener::bind` just fails (or, elsewhere, the app falls back silently) — there is no probe-then-claim step, so stale daemons silently consume ports.

### Proposed fix

Probe ports before claiming; record the chosen port (e.g. in notes.md); sweep leftover daemons at session close.

### Workaround

None found; choose a fallback port manually and `pgrep`-sweep stale daemons by hand.

### Evidence

- First seen 2026-10-11 in `june_3-rebuild` (`docs/photocraft-app-mcp-issues.md`, `docs/session-bug-contract.md` there).

title: Codecs: TIFF IFD walk can be made to spin for seconds with overlapping directory tables (B1)
author: vangel76
body: A TIFF whose thousands of IFDs sit at offsets 4 bytes apart, each declaring 65,535 entries, passes the seen-set (keyed on offset only) and makes every directory parse 65,535 entries, ~6.5e8 iterations per walk, repeated several times per decode. Fix: total entry budget tied to file size.

title: engine.commands unfiltered reply is a bare JSON array
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## What happened

The unfiltered (and filtered) `engine.commands` reply is a top-level JSON array, unlike other control replies which are objects; a consumer assuming `{"commands": [...]}` crashes. Suggested: wrap in an envelope or document the bare-array shape.

## Diagnosis

reply-shape inconsistency (low priority)

## Current shape in the repo (verified 2026-10-11)

- Engine `command.list` returns a bare `Value::Array` — `crates/engine/src/commands.rs:964-976`
- Headless session `command_list()` also returns a bare array — `crates/automation/src/headless.rs:212-226`
- `serve` RPC `engine.commands {filter?}` returns the bare array (filter applied, still an array) as the RPC `result` — `crates/automation/src/rpc.rs:76-92`
- The desktop control channel wraps it in `{"id", "ok": true, "result": [...]}` — `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:376` with `ok()` at `control.rs:133-135` — so the top level is an object, but the `result` field is a bare array rather than `{"commands": [...]}`
- The MCP tool `command_list` emits the bare array as the tool's JSON text output — `crates/automation/src/server.rs:621-646` (`ok_json(&Value::Array(items))`); it defensively accepts both shapes when reading the bridge reply (`server.rs:636-639`)
- `docs/control-protocol.md:46` documents the method but not the reply's bare-array shape

## Suggested fix

Either wrap the list as `{"commands": [...]}` in every transport, or document the bare-array `result` shape in `docs/control-protocol.md` (and keep consumers tolerant of both).

title: PSD: avoid cloning layer data when padding and presize the output buffer (3.1, 3.6)
author: vangel76
body:
`ImageSourceData::to_bytes` (tiff.rs) clones the whole `LayerInfo`, all channel pixel data included, only to call `pad_to`. `PsdFile::to_bytes` (file.rs) starts from an empty Vec and regrows while appending channel data.

Fix: compute the padding length from `unpadded_len` and write the original, and reserve the output size up front. Output must stay byte-identical.

title: Shift+scroll should snap to zoom ladder levels (Photoshop parity)
author: cwshields
body:
## Summary

In Photoshop, holding **Shift** while scrolling (with the *Zoom with Scroll Wheel* preference on) snaps to discrete zoom ladder levels instead of continuous ×1.1 steps. Without the preference, **Shift+Alt+scroll** does the same. PhotoCraft currently lacks this behaviour.

## Expected behaviour

| Modifier | Zoom with Scroll Wheel OFF | Zoom with Scroll Wheel ON |
|---|---|---|
| Scroll | Pan | Continuous ×1.1 zoom |
| Alt+Scroll | Continuous ×1.1 zoom | Pan |
| **Shift+Scroll** | Pan (no change) | **Snap to zoom ladder** |
| **Shift+Alt+Scroll** | **Snap to zoom ladder** | N/A |

Each notch should step to the next/previous level from `zoom_levels::step()`, matching Photoshop's snap behaviour.

## Scope

- Add `SnapZoom(i32)` variant to `wheel_nav::Wheel`
- Track Shift modifier state across wheel gesture frames (like Alt is already tracked)
- Add `snap()` closure to `classify()` for ladder-stepping logic
- Wire `SnapZoom` into the canvas view zoom handler
- Unit tests for all modifier combinations and edge cases (hostile numbers, smoothed tails)

title: Codecs: PNG/WebP allocate the full output buffer from the header before any data is checked (B2)
author: vangel76
body: A ~100 byte PNG declaring 32768x32768 RGBA16 (exactly the default `max_alloc` of 8 GiB) passes `Limits::check_bytes` and then `vec![0u8; size]` asks for 8 GiB before a single IDAT byte is inflated. On Windows, low-RAM machines and wasm32 a failed allocation aborts the process (`handle_alloc_error`), which the shell's `catch_unwind` cannot catch. WebP has the same pattern; only TIFF has a plausibility guard. The wasm32 default `max_alloc` (2 GiB) is also too high.
