title: Shift+scroll wheel should snap to Photoshop zoom ladder levels
author: cwshields
body:
## Problem

Photoshop supports a "snap zoom" modifier: holding **Shift** while scrolling jumps directly to the next discrete zoom ladder level (e.g. 25% → 33.33% → 50% → 66.67% → 100% → 200%) instead of the default continuous ×1.1-per-notch zoom. PhotoCraft's `wheel_nav` module currently only handles continuous zoom (Alt+scroll) and panning (plain scroll), with no snap-to-ladder behaviour.

This matters because designers frequently need to land on exact zoom levels (100% for pixel-accurate work, 50% for overview, 200% for detail) without overshooting or hunting through fractional levels.

## Photoshop behaviour (observed)

| Modifier combo | "Zoom with Scroll Wheel" OFF (default) | "Zoom with Scroll Wheel" ON |
|---|---|---|
| Plain scroll | Pan vertically | Continuous ×1.1 zoom |
| Alt + scroll | Continuous ×1.1 zoom | Pan vertically |
| **Shift + scroll** | Pan sideways (no zoom) | **Snap to next ladder level** |
| **Shift + Alt + scroll** | **Snap to next ladder level** | Pan sideways (no zoom) |
| Shift/Cmd/Ctrl + scroll | Pan sideways | Pan sideways |

Key details:
- Each notch steps exactly one rung on the zoom ladder, positive = zoom in, negative = zoom out
- The smoothed tail of a wheel notch (egui's multi-frame easing) must **not** produce additional snaps or accidental pans
- Shift state must be sticky across gesture frames (same pattern as existing Alt tracking), so releasing Shift mid-tail doesn't change behaviour

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New `Wheel::SnapZoom(i32)` variant in `wheel_nav` for discrete ladder steps
- [ ] `Input` struct gains a `shift: bool` field, tracked across frames via `shift_id()` (same pattern as `alt_id()`)
- [ ] `classify()` returns `SnapZoom` for the correct modifier combinations per the table above
- [ ] Canvas view handler wires `SnapZoom` through `zoom_levels::step()` to reach the exact ladder level
- [ ] Camera Raw preview handles `SnapZoom` gracefully (no-op, since it uses its own zoom scale)
- [ ] Smoothed tails of sna…

title: Faux Bold renders much heavier than Photoshop (PSD import)
author: Lincontrol
body:
**Environment**
- PhotoCraft 0.7.0, Windows
- PSD saved by Photoshop 27.9 (Windows), 3000×3000 px, 11 layers, 3 type layers

**What happens**
Text layers that have Faux Bold enabled in Photoshop look almost identical to the regular font in Photoshop, but in PhotoCraft they come out dramatically heavier. Screenshots attached (Photoshop vs PhotoCraft, same file, same font: Centaur MT Bold / Centaur Italic).

**What I found**
- All three type layers have `/FauxBold true` in their EngineData StyleSheetData, plus `HorizontalScale .62` / `VerticalScale .6`, `FontSize 200` / `220`, `AntiAlias 3`.
- The layer pixels Photoshop stored in the PSD show stem widths close to the plain, non-emboldened font. So Photoshop's faux bold is subtle here.
- PhotoCraft dilates each glyph by `FAUX_BOLD_RADIUS = 0.018` × font size in every direction (`crates/text/src/render.rs`, the 8 offsets in `draw()`), which adds about 3.6% of the em to every stroke.
- The radius uses `face.size_px`, the nominal size, while the offsets are applied in text space, before horizontal/vertical scale. With 60% scaling the dilation is therefore about 1.7× too strong relative to the visible glyph.

**Expected**
Faux Bold on PSD import should look close to Photoshop's own rendering of the same layer.

**Suggestion**
- Scale the faux-bold radius by the effective glyph size (take `horizontal_scale` / `vertical_scale` into account), or apply the offsets after the glyph scale.
- Calibrate `FAUX_BOLD_RADIUS` against Photoshop's stored layer pixels. The rendered pixels in a PSD make a handy reference for a regression test.

title: Windows: opening a PSD from Explorer starts a second PhotoCraft instead of a new tab
author: Lincontrol
body:
**Environment**
- PhotoCraft 0.7.0, Windows
- PhotoCraft set as the default app for `.psd` files

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Start PhotoCraft and open a document.
2. In Windows Explorer, double-click another `.psd` file (or use Open with → PhotoCraft).

**What happens**
A second PhotoCraft window/process starts with the file. You end up with two separate copies of the program, each with its own tabs, panels and memory use.

**Expected**
Like Photoshop: the file opens as a new tab in the PhotoCraft window that is already running. Only start a new instance when PhotoCraft isn't running yet.

**Notes**
- The installer registers `"photocraft.exe" "%1"` as the open command (`packaging/windows/photocraft.wxs`), so Windows launches a new process for every file. I couldn't find any single-instance handling in the app that hands the path to an already running instance.
- A common approach: on startup, try to connect to a named pipe / local socket owned by the running instance. If it exists, send the file path(s), bring that window to the front and exit. Otherwise become the primary instance and listen. Opening several files at once from Explorer should land as tabs in the same window too.
- A setting or `--new-instance` flag to keep the current behaviour would be nice for people who want separate windows.

title: Codecs: Image::convert allocates two f32 buffers for integer depth/layout changes (O1)
author: vangel76
body: `Image::convert` (crates/codecs/src/image.rs) routes every depth or layout change except one through `to_normalized` (4 B/sample f32 Vec), `convert_layout` (another f32 Vec) and `quantize`. It backs `converted()` in every encoder and `to_rgba8()`. A 16-bit RGB image exported to 8-bit JPEG/PNG/BMP peaks at source + 4N + 4N + dest bytes, none of it charged to Limits. Integer U8/U16 conversions that only copy channels (alpha add/drop, gray to RGB, U8 <-> U16) can be done directly with identical output.

title: Codecs: EXR decodes every part to return one, and Cryptomatte skips the cumulative size cap (B3/O2)
author: vangel76
body: `read_layer` used `.all_layers()` then `.nth(index)`, so decoding one part of a multi-part (AOV) EXR decompressed and held every part's pixels; io decodes once per selected part/group, so a 40-AOV file was decoded 40 times. `exr_cryptomatte::decode` did the same and checked parts against `Limits` only individually, not through the cumulative `read_meta` cap, so many large parts could make the `exr` crate preallocate all planes at once. Also the `exr` crate's `rayon` feature was off, so block (de)compression was single-threaded natively.

title: Linux/Xwayland: runaway Undo after XP-Pen shortcut release and pen contact
author: legend914
body:
## Environment
PhotoCraft v0.7.0 (79261615956ab21334e49ca1d384390272e647da), with local UI-only Properties/docking changes; CachyOS Linux, Hyprland, Xwayland. XP-Pen Artist Pro 14 (Gen 2), ACK05 shortcut remote, official PenTablet driver. The remote Undo key is mapped to Ctrl+Z; Redo to Ctrl+Shift+Z.

## User-observed steps
1. Draw several strokes with the tablet.
2. Undo using the tablet/remote shortcut button, then touch the pen to the tablet display.
3. Occasionally PhotoCraft starts undoing consecutive operations even though the shortcut is no longer intentionally held.
4. Undo continues until Ctrl+Z is pressed again.

This is intermittent; exact timing and a deterministic physical-device reproduction are not established. It is not a claim that every pen contact triggers it.

## Expected
A released shortcut must not drain the drawing's undo history. Subsequent pen contact should allow drawing normally.

## Investigation and local mitigation
`crates/ui-egui/src/shortcut_dispatch.rs::dispatch_pressed` dispatches matching pressed Key events without checking `repeat`. egui derives repeat from its held-key set, so a missing release can turn further key-down events into repeated history commands. The independent X11 tablet pressure reader selects pointer events only; it does not synthesize keyboard events.

A synthetic full-app input test models a missing Z release followed by pointer contact and repeated key-down events. This can demonstrate the unbounded-history behavior, but does not establish whether the physical trigger originates in the XP-Pen driver, compositor/Xwayland, winit, or the app input path.

A local protective patch discards repeat events for the effective Undo/Redo bindings before history/tool handlers run, while keeping fresh presses and unrelated repeating shortcuts. It changes hold-to-repeat Undo/Redo to one operation per fresh key press. Physical-device confirmation is still needed; this mitigation alone does not repair a stuck Ctrl modifier upst…

title: Pen tool: Shift constrains segments and handles to 45° (TOOL-214-10)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #214 (scorecard TOOL-214-10, docs/gaps.md G5).

**What's missing on main:** the Pen tool ignores Shift. `pen_down` / `pen_move` in `crates/ui-egui/src/vector_ui.rs` place anchors and pull handles at the raw pointer position. Alt (break handle), Ctrl/Cmd (Direct Selection), Backspace and the close-drag are done (#790, #1466, #3306); "no Shift 45 deg" is the last open part of the row.

**Photoshop:** holding Shift while clicking the next anchor constrains the new segment to the nearest multiple of 45° from the previous anchor; holding Shift while dragging out direction handles constrains the handle to multiples of 45° (refs: https://photoshoptrainingchannel.com/tips/straight-lines-creating-paths/, https://community.adobe.com/t5/photoshop-ecosystem-discussions/how-to-set-constrained-angles-while-drawing-and-holding-shift/m-p/12629626/highlight/true).

**Proposal:**
- Shift at the press snaps the new anchor's angle from the previous anchor to 45° steps (keeping the distance); Shift during the drag snaps the handle direction around its anchor to 45° steps. Pure gesture state (the path is committed through the existing `path.*` command on Enter / close), so no new command.
- Unit tests in `vector_ui.rs`: Shift-click at ~30° lands on 45°; Shift-drag handle snaps; without Shift unchanged; first anchor unaffected.
- Flip TOOL-214-10 in `scorecard/*.toml` if nothing else remains.

title: Character panel: OpenType feature buttons (TYPE-218-5)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #218 (scorecard TYPE-218-5, docs/gaps.md G8).

**What's missing on main:** the OpenType features are reachable only through Type › OpenType (`type.openType.*`, `crates/engine/src/type_extra_cmds.rs`). The Character panel (`crates/ui-egui/src/type_tool.rs` `character_panel`) has no OpenType button row.

**Photoshop:** the Character panel has a row of OpenType toggle buttons at the bottom: Standard Ligatures, Contextual Alternates, Discretionary Ligatures, Swash, Stylistic Alternates, Titling Alternates, Ordinals, Fractions; each shows on/off for the selected text and toggles the feature (refs: https://www.breathingcolor.com/blogs/news/photoshop-typography-elements-of-the-character-panel-part-2, https://support.fontspring.com/hc/en-us/articles/10243535439899-How-to-Access-OpenType-Features-in-Photoshop).

**Proposal:**
- Add the eight toggle buttons to the Character panel, dispatching the existing `type.openType.*` command ids (no new commands); the pressed state reads the active text run's features. Tooltips with the feature names, colours from `theme::Tokens`.
- UI test (the panel dispatches the command and the state reflects the layer), snapshot check.
- Numerals and Stylistic Sets submenus are not part of this issue (row stays partial).

title: Batch: Include All Subfolders (AUTO-219-5)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #219 (scorecard AUTO-219-5, docs/gaps.md G11).

**What's missing on main:** the batch commands (`crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs`, `"input"`: folder or array of files) only list the top level of a folder; files in subfolders are skipped.

**Photoshop:** File › Automate › Batch has an **Include All Subfolders** option that also processes files in subdirectories of the specified source folder (Adobe help: https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/desktop/automate-tasks/process-a-batch-of-files/batch-and-droplet-processing-options.html).

**Proposal:**
- New optional param `"includeSubfolders": bool = false` on the batch commands that take a folder `input`; recursion is bounded (depth limit + seen-set against symlink loops), order deterministic. Outputs keep the relative subfolder path under `output` (created as needed) so same-named files in different subfolders don't collide.
- Checkbox "Include All Subfolders" in the Batch dialog.
- Tests: nested folders processed, default unchanged, bad param type -> Err, symlink/depth guard; `panic_hunt`.
- Naming template, progress/cancel stay open (row stays partial).

title: Pattern Stamp, Spot Healing Brush and Background Eraser draw live (TOOL-213-7)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #213 (scorecard TOOL-213-7, docs/gaps.md G4).

**What's missing on main:** `strokes_live` / `live_retouch_command` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` draw Brush, Pencil, Eraser, Blur, Sharpen, Smudge, Dodge, Burn, Sponge, Clone Stamp, Healing Brush and History Brush live. **Pattern Stamp, Spot Healing Brush and Background Eraser** still show nothing until release. (Mixer Brush is handled in #3627 and is not part of this issue.)

**Photoshop:** these tools paint during the drag, like every other brush-based tool.

**Proposal:**
- Route the three tools through the live-stroke path (`LiveRetouch` with `paint.patternStamp`, `paint.spotHealing`, `paint.backgroundEraser`), so the release commits the same pixels the live stroke showed, one history step, as for Clone Stamp (P32). Where a tool's final result needs the whole stroke (Spot Healing blends after release in Photoshop too), show the live stroke and finish on release as the Healing Brush does.
- Tests: live result equals the committed result for each tool; mask/channel targeting kept; no change for the already-live tools.

title: PSD: version 3 Photo Filter layers are not read (color decoded as Lab instead of XYZ)
author: detunized
body:
PhotoCraft 0.7.0, macOS.

All 145 PSDs in my archive that have a Photo Filter adjustment layer (made in Photoshop CS2, 2005 to 2007) open with this warning:

```
warning: layer "Photo Filter 1": its Photo Filter settings could not be read; the layer is kept as saved but has no effect
```

They render noticeably cooler than in Photoshop.

![Photoshop vs PhotoCraft 0.7.0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d2385ae-bb54-4da2-a00b-a3ddba586935)

The `phfl` block in `deathvalley03.psd`:

```
00 03  00 00 5e 7f  00 00 61 aa  00 00 0e f3  00 00 00 3f  01 00
```

That's version 3, then three u32 values (24191, 25002, 3827), density 63 and Preserve Luminosity on.

`parse_photo_filter` in `crates/io/src/adjust_map.rs` reads version 3 as Lab × 100. That makes L = 241.91, which is out of range, so the layer becomes Unsupported. Adobe's PSD spec describes version 3 as "4 bytes each for XYZ color". The values do look like XYZ: chromaticity x ≈ 0.456, y ≈ 0.472, a warm yellow orange, which matches how the photo looks in Photoshop. I don't know the exact scaling of the three values.

**Repro**

```
photocraft-cli info deathvalley03-small.psd           # "Photo Filter 1" is Unsupported
photocraft-cli convert deathvalley03.psd photocraft.jpg
```

Stack: Curves > Photo Filter (Multiply, 33% fill) > Background.

**Expected:** close to Photoshop's export.
**Actual:** mean absolute difference 8.5 of 255 at full size, with a mean RGB offset of −10.5, −1.3, +12.3, so too blue. Files with only Curves layers render within about 1 of Photoshop, so the difference comes from the missing filter.

Side note: the warning says the layer "has no effect", but the layer is still blended in its Multiply mode. That fallback is actually closer to Photoshop than skipping the layer would be (8.5 vs 23 off), so only the wording is off.

**Attached**
- [deathvalley03-small-900px.psd.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33313893/deathvalley03-small-900px.psd.zip): 900×600 copy resized and s…

title: Flatten Image changes the pixel values of a CMYK document
author: detunized
body:
PhotoCraft 0.7.0, macOS.

With a 16 bit CMYK PSD (profile U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2), Layer › Flatten Image changes the colors. It happens even when the document has only a Background layer.

![Photoshop, PhotoCraft render, PhotoCraft after Flatten Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43e90e68-0080-4a39-aa02-f793f9ddfd0b)

**Repro**

```
photocraft-cli convert container.psd render.jpg
photocraft-cli run container.psd --cmd layer.flattenImage --out flattened.jpg
```

Stack: Curves > Background.

- `render.jpg` matches Photoshop: mean absolute difference 3.0 of 255 against Photoshop's own export.
- `flattened.jpg` is 20.0 off, with a mean RGB offset of +5.1, +26.3, +27.2, so lighter and bluer.

**Flattening alone is enough**

Deleting the Curves layer first (`--cmd layer.delete --params '{"layer":3}'`) leaves only the Background layer, and flattening still changes the result by 12.4 of 255.

Mean channel values of the saved PSD before and after flattening (as stored, read with psd-tools):

| | C | M | Y | K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 0.706 | 0.756 | 0.775 | 0.946 |
| after | 0.748 | 0.834 | 0.861 | 0.940 |

The embedded profile is kept.

**Expected:** flattening a document with one layer leaves the pixels unchanged.

**Attached**
- [container-small.psd.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33313873/container-small.psd.zip): 750×500 copy resized and saved by PhotoCraft. It reproduces all of the above. The original is 41 MB, over the attachment limit.

title: [High][Data loss] Flatten All Layer Effects deletes layer and vector masks, including disabled masks
author: shmuelbiller1
body:
[High][Data loss] Flatten All Layer Effects deletes layer and vector masks, including disabled masks
Reproduction
1. Create a raster layer with a nontrivial raster or vector mask. Disable the mask and note its contents.
2. Enable an editable effect (e.g., Color Overlay).
3. Run File → Scripts → Flatten All Layer Effects (file.scripts.flattenAllLayerEffects).
4. Inspect the mask and save/reopen the result.
Expected
Flatten the effects without destroying unrelated mask data, including disabled masks.
Source evidence
- crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs:1056-1075: flatten_all_effects bakes and then unconditionally does l.mask = None and l.vector_mask = None.
- crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs:1036-1050: bake renders a clone.
- crates/doc/src/lib.rs:235-241: disabled raster masks return 1.0 and are not baked into the pixels.
- crates/engine/src/file_cmds/tests.rs:514-555: current test flattens effects before adding a mask; never checks a layer with both together.
Impact
Destruction of editable mask geometry/pixels and state; persistent after save/close. Undo may recover immediately.
Fix and verification
Bake effect visuals without double-applying masks; preserve original mask objects and state. Regression tests with enabled/disabled raster and vector masks, compositing equality, undo/redo, and .pcraft roundtrip.

title: [High][Data loss] In-place Save of OpenRaster omits adjustment layers and marks file clean
author: shmuelbiller1
body:
[High][Data loss] In-place Save of OpenRaster omits adjustment layers and marks file clean
Reproduction
1. Open an existing layered .ora file in PhotoCraft.
2. Create an adjustment layer (e.g. Curves) and make a visually obvious adjustment.
3. Use File → Save to save back to the .ora file.
4. Close/reopen and inspect the Layers panel and composite.
Expected
Either preserve all editable layers, or require explicit confirmation / Save As in a lossless format before a destructive overwrite. Do not mark document clean after silently losing adjustment-layer editability.
Source evidence
- crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs:153-168: saves_in_place calls layered_extension, and layered_extension explicitly includes ora. Thus an opened ORA is eligible for direct in-place File → Save, notwithstanding an outdated comment that lists only PSD/PSB/.pcraft.
- crates/io/src/ora.rs:604-624: ORA exporter explicitly skips every adjustment layer and emits a warning.
- crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1248-1257,1272-1282: Save retrieves the active ORA path using saves_in_place; Save As also treats .ora as a layered destination, rather than a copy.
- crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1301-1364: after writing, the save completion marks the document saved and only then presents export warnings.
Impact
Ordinary File → Save on an existing ORA, or Save As to an existing ORA path, can overwrite an editable original with a file lacking adjustment layers; the merged preview retains the rendered look but the adjustment operations are permanently missing from the file. This is a destructive format conversion not enforced by a pre-write confirmation.
Fix and verification
Treat ORA as non-lossless when unsupported features exist, preserving source identity and dirty state (Save a Copy semantics). Before overwriting a file, warn about adjustments/effects/masks/metadata and require affirmative opt-in. title: [Feature Request] Add comprehensive Aseprite (.ase/.aseprite) import and export support
author: jjhaggar
body:
## Summary

I'd like to propose adding **comprehensive, bidirectional support for Aseprite's native `.ase` / `.aseprite` format**, allowing PhotoCraft to import, edit, save, and export pixel-art documents and animated sprites.

The goal is **high-fidelity interoperability**, preserving layers, groups, indexed colors, palettes, animation, and document metadata wherever possible, rather than flattening everything into a single raster image.

This would complement the ongoing discussion about additional file formats in #3692.

Aseprite's binary format is publicly documented, and an independent Rust library already provides reading and writing capabilities. This could make comprehensive support considerably easier to implement.

The proposal below distinguishes **essential functionality**, **optional advanced features**, and **general compatibility requirements**. The intention is to achieve the broadest practical format coverage without requiring PhotoCraft to reproduce every specialized editing tool in Aseprite.

## 1. Essential Features (High Priority)

These are the main capabilities that would make Aseprite support genuinely useful.

### Color Modes and Palettes

- [ ] **RGBA (32 bpp):** preserve RGB values and per-pixel alpha.
- [ ] **Grayscale (16 bpp):** preserve grayscale values and alpha.
- [ ] **Indexed color (8 bpp):** preserve original palette indices and transparency, not just the rendered RGB colors.
- [ ] Preserve palette entries, RGBA values, color names, transparent indices, and palette changes across frames where applicable.
- [ ] Preserve relevant color profiles (sRGB, ICC, gamma) and document properties such as pixel aspect ratio.

**Important:** Indexed-color fidelity deserves particular attention. Converting indexed pixels to RGB and then rebuilding the palette can change their original indices even when the resulting image looks identical.

Ideally, indexed images should remain genuinely indexed throughout import, editing, and export whenever pos…

title: Windows: physical RAM is never detected, so the GPU budget assumes 16 GB, and the 8 GB-per-document default isn't scaled to the machine
author: greg5552
body:
I'm a sign-shop designer evaluating PhotoCraft on a Windows 11 laptop. These observations come from reading the source with AI help. **I haven't reproduced an out-of-memory failure in the app yet**, so please treat this as a code-reading report.

**1. Windows never reports physical RAM.** In `crates/ui-egui/src/gpu_canvas.rs`, `detect_physical_memory()` has implementations for macOS, Linux and FreeBSD. The fallback `#[cfg(not(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "linux", target_os = "freebsd")))]` returns `None`, and that fallback is what Windows gets. The GPU compositor budget is `min(Memory Usage − pixels, RAM/4)` with a 512 MB floor, so on Windows it falls back to an assumed 16 GB and allows up to 4 GB. On integrated graphics that comes out of system RAM.

**2. The Memory Usage default is fixed at 8,192 MB per document** (`crates/engine/src/prefs.rs`, `memory_usage_mb: 8192`), whatever the machine has. Two open documents can each keep 8 GB of history before anything is trimmed. On a 16 GB machine that's the whole machine.

**3. No spill to disk.** The Scratch Disks preference is editable in the UI, but your scorecard already lists `scratch_disks.disks` as unread. A user who sees that panel will reasonably assume PhotoCraft spills to disk the way Photoshop does.

**Suggestions:**
- Detect RAM on Windows (for example through the `sysinfo` crate, or `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` via `windows-sys`).
- Default Memory Usage to a share of installed RAM rather than a fixed 8 GB.
- Until spilling exists, mark the Scratch Disks panel "not yet implemented" so it doesn't suggest a safety net that isn't there.

Context: #212 (out-of-memory recovery), #1015 (GPU out of memory on large documents), #1637 (headless memory peak). Thanks for the remarkable work.

title: Crop tool: Content-Aware fill of the area a rotated or extended crop uncovers
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #1919 (Crop tool tracker): the unchecked item *"Content-Aware fill of the empty corners after rotating or extending the canvas"*. Listed as `partial` in `docs/ui-parity.md` ("Content-Aware crop fill").

## What Photoshop does

The Crop tool's options bar has a **Content-Aware** checkbox. With it on, when committing a crop that is rotated (Straighten, or turning the frame) or that extends past the canvas, the area the image doesn't cover is filled from its surroundings instead of with the background colour / transparency. This is the classic patch-based Content-Aware fill, not a generative one. Undo removes crop and fill in one step.

## Why it's small

The fill engine already exists and is used by Edit › Fill › Content-Aware:
- `crates/algo/src/inpaint.rs` (PatchMatch completion) and `crates/algo/src/content_aware.rs` (sampling window, colour adaptation)
- `crates/engine/src/fill_cmds.rs` (`content_aware`, `sampling_window`, `window_size`)

`image.crop` already runs a rotated crop as one compound step (`rotated_crop` in `crates/engine/src/image_cmds.rs`: rotate arbitrary, then crop).

## Proposed

1. **Engine:** `image.crop` gains `"contentAware": bool = false`. When on, after the rotate/crop and inside the same compound undo step, build the mask of uncovered pixels (rotation corners plus any extended canvas) and fill it on the layer the crop filled (Background) with the existing content-aware path. Also for an unrotated crop that extends the canvas.
2. **Per hole:** fill each connected piece of the mask (each corner / edge strip) with its own sampling window; one window around the union bbox would be the whole canvas.
3. **Failure:** too little image to sample from, or a window too large → `Err` with a clear message, document unchanged.
4. **UI:** "Content-Aware" checkbox in the Crop options bar (`crates/ui-egui/src/crop_ui.rs`), state in `state.rs`, passed to `image.crop`. Match Photoshop's enable rules (e.g. its interaction with Delete Cropped Pixels): ch…

title: Add Anchor Point inserts away from the hit position on straight segments
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
### Summary

Adding an anchor to a straight path can insert it away from the position returned by hit testing (and displayed by the hover preview).

### Environment

- PhotoCraft source: `886372812d71c1d73d757ada2f0a0d47d613f3ed` (`main`, version 0.7.0)
- Windows x86_64, Rust 1.99.0, default Cargo test profile/features
- Reproduced with the shared vector editing API; this report does not claim a manual desktop UI test.

### Reproduction

1. Construct a straight, open `Subpath::polyline(&[(0.0, 0.0), (100.0, 0.0)])` inside a `Path`.
2. Call `photocraft_vector::edit::hit` at `(15.625, 0.0)`, with tolerance `1.0` and no visible handles.
3. It returns `Hit::Segment([0, 0], 0.25)`.
4. Pass the returned knot and parameter directly to `edit::add_anchor`.

**Expected:** the new anchor is at `(15.625, 0.0)`.

**Actual:** the new anchor is at `(25.0, 0.0)`, 9.375 pixels away.

The canvas anchor tool forwards the hit-test parameter to `path.addAnchor`, and its hover preview evaluates the cubic at that same parameter.

### Cause and proposed fix

[`add_anchor`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/886372812d71c1d73d757ada2f0a0d47d613f3ed/crates/vector/src/edit.rs#L190) uses linear interpolation for a segment with retracted handles. Hit testing evaluates it as a cubic with controls `[start, start, end, end]`; its curve parameter is not linear distance along the line.

Evaluating the same cubic when locating the new corner aligns insertion with hit testing. The new anchor can still have retracted handles, preserving the straight path.

I have a small fix and a failing regression covering horizontal, vertical, diagonal, and closing segments at non-midpoint parameters. Nearby open PRs #2824 and #3464 do not change this insertion calculation.

Investigated with Codex assistance; the regression failure was executed locally.

title: Free Transform clips signed/HDR color samples in 32-bit float layers
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
### Summary

An integer translation of a 32-bit floating-point layer clips color samples outside `[0, 1]`. Highlights above 1 and negative values are lost even though translation should preserve them.

### Environment

- PhotoCraft source: `886372812d71c1d73d757ada2f0a0d47d613f3ed` (`main`, version 0.7.0)
- Windows x86_64, Rust 1.99.0, default Cargo test profile/features
- Reproduced through the Rust transform API; the desktop UI was not used for this reproduction.

### Reproduction

Create an `RGBA32F` `Surface`, fill a small rectangle with `[2.0, -0.25, 0.5, 0.5]`, then call `photocraft_algo::transform::warp_surface` with a translation homography:

```rust
Homography([1.0, 0.0, 7.0, 0.0, 1.0, -3.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
```

Read an interior pixel at the translated position. The same clipping occurs with nearest-neighbor, bilinear, and bicubic interpolation. The engine's `edit.transform` command uses this routine through `transform_layer`.

**Expected:** `[2.0, -0.25, 0.5, 0.5]`.

**Actual:** `[1.0, 0.0, 0.5, 0.5]`.

A half-pixel bilinear translation also clips interpolated HDR values: a regression expecting `[3.0, -0.375, 0.5, 0.5]` returns `[1.0, 0.0, 0.5, 0.5]`.

### Cause and proposed fix

[`warp_surface`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/886372812d71c1d73d757ada2f0a0d47d613f3ed/crates/algo/src/transform.rs#L371) unconditionally clamps the unpremultiplied color channels. Destination sample storage already clips U8/U16 and preserves F32. Removing this extra color clamp should preserve floating-point range while retaining the alpha clamp.

I have a small fix and regression tests covering RGB/grayscale, all three depths, alpha/no-alpha, and fractional interpolation. Searches of issues and PRs found no matching transform report; #2592 addresses related float-range preservation in different operations.

Investigated with Codex assistance; the regression failures were executed locally.

title: CLI run exits successfully and exports after a recorded action fails
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
### Summary

`photocraft-cli run --cmd actions.play` treats a failed recorded action as success. It executes later commands, writes `--out`, and exits with status 0. CLI `batch` already checks this failure result.

### Environment

- PhotoCraft `886372812d71c1d73d757ada2f0a0d47d613f3ed`, version 0.7.0
- Windows x86_64, Rust 1.99.0, default Cargo test/dev profile and features
- Reproduced using the CLI executable and an integration test

### Reproduction

Run this in an empty temporary directory:

```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":8,"height":8}' --cmd layer.new.layer --cmd actions.record --params '{"name":"Delete"}' --cmd layer.delete --cmd actions.stop --cmd actions.play --params '{"action":"Delete"}' --cmd document.inspect --out result.png
```

This creates two layers, records deleting one, then replays the deletion with only one layer remaining. The action cannot delete the final layer.

**Expected:** a nonzero exit code with an action/step diagnostic, no subsequent `document.inspect`, and no `result.png` export.

**Actual:** status 0, empty stderr, `document.inspect` output, and `result.png` exists. The action result on stdout contains:

```json
{"action":"Delete","failed":{"error":"a document must keep at least one layer","id":"layer.delete","step":0},"ran":0}
```

### Proposed fix

Check `photocraft_engine::actions_cmds::nested_failure` in `run_cmds` after `command_run`, as the CLI's batch path already does. The engine intentionally returns structured playback failure information; callers must promote it to a CLI failure.

Related fixes #2783 and #2792 handle engine scripting/batch and CLI batch respectively. This report concerns the separate `run` path. I have a small fix with failure and successful-playback integration tests.

Investigated with Codex assistance; the failure and unexpected export were executed and verified locally.

title: History byte budget omits off-playhead video frames and original footage
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
History's pixel-memory accounting visits a video layer's displayed surface but omits the rest of its frame stack and original footage. Undo snapshots retain those omitted tiles, so deleting off-playhead frames can exceed the history byte budget without triggering eviction.

Affected baseline: `6de37ce7f063e6814903650a24c8dad4936e8136`.

### Synthetic reproduction

Create a video layer with six independently allocated frames and display frame 0. Delete four other frames in separate history steps. The current document holds two frames and history retains the four deleted frames.

Expected: `History::pixel_bytes` accounts for all six unique frame allocations, `unique_bytes` accounts for the four retained only by history, and a three-frame budget discards the three oldest states while keeping the latest step undoable.

Actual: the visitor sees only the displayed frame, so the byte count underreports and the four states are retained.

`crates/ops/src/tiles.rs::surfaces` should also visit `VideoData::frames` and `original_frames`. Existing tile-pointer deduplication can avoid double-counting the displayed frame and unchanged original footage shared through copy-on-write.

Tests cover U8/U16/F32, original/altered/displayed aliases, rasterizing a video layer, undo/redo accounting, and budget eviction. This is separate from #3614, which addresses selection-mask tiles.

title: Feathered selections mix filter colors incorrectly when alpha changes
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Applying a transparency-changing filter through a feathered selection mixes straight color and alpha independently, producing incorrect edge colors.

Affected baseline: `6de37ce7f063e6814903650a24c8dad4936e8136`.

### Minimal example

Use an opaque RGB pixel `[0.5,0.5,0.5,1]`, a selection coverage of `0.5`, and Color to Alpha removing white with the default thresholds.

The fully filtered result is black at alpha 0.5. The current selection mixer produces `[0.25,0.25,0.25,0.75]`. Composited over white, that becomes 0.4375 instead of the original 0.5. Premultiplied interpolation gives color 1/3 at alpha 0.75, preserving the original appearance over the removed color.

The same problem affects Offset through a partial selection: moving opaque blue into a transparent pixel whose hidden color is red produces purple instead of blue at reduced coverage.

The shared `mix_selection` in `crates/algo/src/lib.rs` linearly interpolates each stored channel independently. It needs alpha-aware interpolation when alpha changes, while retaining ordinary scalar interpolation for surfaces without alpha and filters that preserve alpha.

Regression tests exercise RGB and grayscale, 8/16/32-bit samples, partial input alpha, and multiple selection coverages. This is a general selection-mixing issue rather than the transform sampling issue in #3853.

title: Deleting an earlier alpha channel redirects edits away from the surviving target
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Deleting an alpha channel can change the edit target to Composite even when the targeted channel survives. It also loses the final surviving channel's visibility flag.

Reproduced on `6de37ce7f063e6814903650a24c8dad4936e8136`, Windows x86_64, using engine command tests.

### Reproduction

1. Create a document.
2. Run `channel.new` with `{"name":"Remove","fill":"black"}`.
3. Run `channel.new` with `{"name":"Keep","fill":"white"}`. Keep is now the target.
4. Run `channel.delete` with `{"channel":"Remove"}`.
5. Run `image.adjustments.invert` with `{}`.

Expected: Keep remains selected and visible, and Invert modifies Keep only.

Actual: Keep survives at index 0, but the target becomes Composite and its eye is lost; subsequent implicit edits can modify the layer instead. With three channels, removing a middle channel also loses the last channel's eye independently of which channel is targeted.

`Session::edit` calls `fix_view` after shrinking the channel list. This truncates `alpha_visible` and resets an out-of-range target before `delete_channel` can remap the old indices. Preserve the pre-edit channel view until the deletion succeeds, then remap and validate it against the new list.

The regression covers 8/16/32-bit documents, surviving targets on both sides of the deletion, deleting the target, distinct visibility flags, and an implicit edit followed by undo/redo. Channel view itself remains non-historical, as documented by the module.

title: [FEATURE REQUEST] Blend RGB Colors Using Gamma
author: ericclii
body:
• Standard sRGB Blending (Gamma ~2.2): Standard computer images are encoded in sRGB, which follows a non-linear curve matching human eye perception. When you blend colors directly in sRGB space (like mixing red and green at 50% opacity), the mid-tones can look dark, muddy, or create a dark "sludge" border.
• Linear Blending: Enabling a gamma value of 1.0 converts colors into a mathematically linear color space before mixing. This produces physically accurate light behavior, brighter and smoother gradient transitions, and yellow-ish or lighter natural overlaps instead of dark muddy edges.

title: web build: the wasm exceeds the 24 MiB size gate (25,516,128 bytes)
author: dottedt
body:
### What happened

The `web build and wasm size gate` CI job fails on `main` (and so on every PR whose `platforms` job marks web-relevant):

```
photocraft-web-..._bg.wasm: 25516128 bytes (24 MiB; limit 25165824)
error: ... is 25516128 bytes, over the 25165824-byte limit (Cloudflare's per-file cap is 25 MiB)
```

### Numbers

- Gate: `packaging/web/package.sh`, `MAX_WASM_BYTES=25165824` (24 MiB), intentionally below Cloudflare's 25 MiB per-file cap so a regression shows up before upload.
- Now: 25,516,128 bytes (over the gate by 350,304; still under Cloudflare's 26,214,400 by ~698 KB).
- Baseline recorded 2026-10-06 in `crates/text/build.rs`: 24,190,076 bytes, so the wasm has grown ~1.33 MB.

### Impact

The web job is red on `main`, so it is red on every web-relevant PR. It is a size regression, not a build break: the artifact builds and runs.

### Fix

Either trim the ~1.33 MB of growth (preferable; the gate exists to catch exactly this), or, if the growth is intentional and unavoidable, raise `MAX_WASM_BYTES` to Cloudflare's 25 MiB cap with a comment and a new baseline. The build profile and per-crate wasm exclusions are in `Cargo.toml` (the wasm release profile) and `crates/text/Cargo.toml` (ICU dictionary data is native only).

### Evidence

- `packaging/web/package.sh` lines 27-40; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `web:` job; the CI job output above.

- [ ] Tamil typing works with supported external input tools.

- [ ] Text layers remain editable without character corruption.
- [ ] Saved projects preserve Tamil text.
- [ ] Exported images display Tamil correctly.

**What happens**

`cargo xtask corpus --all` (run by CI's `corpus` job on every PR and on main, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:184`) fetches PngSuite like this:

- `xtask/src/corpus_pins.rs:42`: `PNGSUITE_URL = "http://www.schaik.com/pngsuite/PngSuite-2017jul19.tgz"`
- `xtask/src/corpus.rs:179-186`: `curl -fsSL` to that URL, then `tar -xzf` into `corpus/pngsuite/`, then the archive is deleted.

Nothing checks a hash at any point. The only gate is "at least 175 `.png` files present" (`corpus.rs:174`). Every other corpus goes through `PinnedCorpus` with a manifest in `xtask/*.sha256`; PngSuite has no manifest. So a cached `corpus/` restore is not verified for PngSuite either.

**Why it matters**

- The download is plain HTTP, so anything on the network path can swap the archive. Its contents are unpacked by `tar` and then fed to the PNG decoder tests in CI.
- The docs say it is verified:
  - `AGENTS.md:109` says PngSuite is "fetched at pinned commits and sha256-verified by `cargo xtask corpus --all`".
  - `ci.yml:157-158` and the `cargo xtask corpus` help text (`corpus.rs:127`) say the same.
- schaik.com does not serve HTTPS (the TLS handshake fails as of 2026-10-11), so changing the URL to https is not a fix on its own.

**Suggested fix**

Either of these:

1. Add a `PNGSUITE_SHA256` pin next to `PNGSUITE_URL` and verify the archive before `tar` runs. Also include it in the CI cache key.
2. Mirror the 2017jul19 archive into storytold/photocraft-corpus and fetch it through the existing `PinnedCorpus` path, like the other corpora. This also removes the dependency on a third-party HTTP host.

Test and CI only; the shipped app does not download anything. Seen on `main` at `afac33f8d7`.

title: Group transforms use selection-clipped bounds while moving the whole group
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
When a pixel selection is active, transforming a group calculates its starting frame from selected portions of its raster children, but applies the resulting transform to the whole group. This can produce the wrong size or rotation center; a selection outside the group's content makes an otherwise valid transform fail.

Reproduction on `c20b81b25168057e9cbffa2f45c36ec02dacf756`:
1. Put a 20×10 raster layer at (10,10) inside a group and select the group.
2. Make a 5×5 selection at (10,10).
3. Transform the group to the quad (10,10), (50,10), (50,30), (10,30).

Expected: the group's full 20×10 frame scales to 40×20. Actual: the frame is taken from the 5×5 selection, while the whole child is scaled, producing 160×40. With a selection outside the group, the command reports nothing to transform. Rotate/flip presets also use the incorrect frame.

`transform_bounds` recursively applies the document selection to raster descendants even though `moves_whole(group)` and the group transform implementation explicitly operate on the whole group. The fix should apply selection clipping only for the originally requested layer when it supports selected-pixel transforms, retaining whole-content bounds for group descendants.

This is separate from the multi-layer transform work in #3597 and Skew interaction work in #3590. It is an internal bounds/operation mismatch; no claim of direct Photoshop testing.


A focused fix and regression tests are prepared; I am completing the repository validation gates before submitting the PR.

title: Profileless grayscale exports skip color conversion and change brightness
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Exporting a grayscale document with a non-default ICC profile to a format that cannot embed that profile can change its appearance. `export_flat` converts profiled RGB to the untagged destination encoding, but skips the equivalent grayscale conversion before stripping the profile.

Reproduced on `c20b81b25168057e9cbffa2f45c36ec02dacf756` with a synthetic linear-gray ICC document and TGA export. An 8-bit input near linear 0.25 decodes from the exported TGA as 0.2509804; the corresponding sGray value is approximately 0.5380651. Thus a normal untagged interpretation is visibly too dark.

Expected: use the document's grayscale profile to convert samples to the destination's untagged sGray encoding when the output cannot retain ICC. Keep the existing behavior for default/untagged sGray, alpha, and outputs that can embed the profile.

The existing `convert_gray` helper already handles the inverse direction for linear HDR/EXR output. This is the missing grayscale branch beside `convert_rgb` for formats without ICC support. This report concerns PhotoCraft's documented/default color encoding and an independent transfer-function check, not a claim of direct Photoshop testing.


A focused fix and regression tests are prepared; I am completing the repository validation gates before submitting the PR.

title: Filter previews lose selected channel targets and show stale channel overlays
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Generic filter previews do not consistently preserve the channel being edited. Their temporary engine Session selects the active layer but starts with the default composite channel target. The final command uses the real session's target. In addition, channel-view overlays read the committed document instead of the filtered preview.

Reproduction on `c20b81b25168057e9cbffa2f45c36ec02dacf756`:
1. Create an alpha channel with a hard black/white edge and select it in Channels.
2. Open Gaussian Blur and increase the radius with Preview enabled.
3. Compare the displayed edge before OK with the committed edge after OK.

Expected: Preview shows the edit to the selected channel, and turning Preview off or cancelling restores the original view without changing the document. The same target must be used by preview and commit.

Actual: the alpha-channel overlay continues to display the original edge. The temporary preview session can filter layer pixels instead of the selected alpha channel. A selected color channel similarly loses its edit restriction in the temporary session.

This concerns the preview target and displayed document, distinct from Sharpen proxy-resolution issue #3929 / PR #3936 and generic dialog presentation PR #3877.


A focused fix and regression tests are prepared; I am completing the repository validation gates before submitting the PR.

title: Touch scrolling conflicts with drag-and-drop in preset browsers
author: MXJinjing
body:
## Observed behavior

While using PhotoCraft on a physical HarmonyOS tablet through [my native HarmonyOS fork](https://github.com/MXJinjing/photocraft-hmos), I encountered conflicts between scrolling and drag-and-drop in preset browsers:

- A one-finger swipe over a preset could start dragging it instead of scrolling the list.
- After an initial local attempt to require a double-press gesture, intentional drags still became scrolling on the physical device.
- The brush picker has the same interaction problem for presets, group headers, and nested-folder headers.

The relevant shared UI uses egui `Sense::click_and_drag()` inside scroll areas. These observations are from the HarmonyOS port; behavior on upstream desktop/web builds still needs verification.

## Interaction implemented in the fork

For touch/pen, a normal swipe scrolls. To drag, tap and release an item, then press the same item again within 0.5 seconds and move while keeping that second press held. There is no additional long-press delay. Mouse input retains direct press-and-drag.

This policy was chosen for the fork. Upstream maintainers may prefer another gesture or different touch/pen policies.

## Implementation and lessons learned

- A shared gate tracks item identity, input source, tap timing, and movement, with touch/pen tolerances independent of egui's mouse click tolerance.
- The last contact position survives release events containing `PointerGone`, so lifting a finger does not lose the first tap's position.
- On the matching second press, drag ownership is explicitly transferred to the item's actual widget ID with `ctx.set_dragged_id()`. Switching the item's sense on a later frame alone left the scroll area owning the gesture, because egui had selected a potential drag target using the previous frame's widget senses.
- The armed gesture suppresses the long-touch context-menu response and retains drag ownership through the release frame.

title: Feature Request: Add Nix / NixOS packaging support (flake.nix)
author: lebarde
body:
### Summary

Would you consider adding upstream packaging support for Nix and NixOS (e.g., via a `flake.nix` or a `default.nix` file) to the repository?

### Context & Motivation

NixOS relies on a declarative, reproducible package manager that does not adhere to the standard Filesystem Hierarchy Standard (FHS). Dynamic linkers and libraries are not located in `/lib` or `/usr/lib`, which means generic Linux binaries or standard build scripts often require patching (`patchelf` or `buildFHSEnv`) to run properly on Nix systems.

Providing an upstream Nix configuration would offer several benefits:
- **Zero-setup installation**: Users on Nix/NixOS could run or install the application directly via `nix run github:organization/project` or by importing the flake into their system configuration.
- **Reproducible development environments**: A `devShell` in the flake would guarantee that contributors have the exact same toolchains and dependency versions, regardless of their host distribution.
- **Continuous Integration**: Nix derivations can be integrated into GitHub Actions to verify builds against pinned, hermetic environments.

### Proposed Solution

1. Add a `flake.nix` (and optionally a `flake.lock`) at the project root defining:
   - The package derivation (handling build dependencies and wrapping runtime assets/libraries).
   - An application output (`apps.default`) so users can test it with `nix run`.
   - A development shell (`devShells.default`) containing all build prerequisites.
2. Maintain this derivation alongside regular releases, or keep it lightweight so external contributors can help maintain it.

### Additional Context

If you are open to this, I would be happy to prepare and submit a Pull Request providing an initial `flake.nix` for you to review.

title: [Bug]: Paint Bucket canvas cursor is a crosshair, not a paint bucket
author: LimitlessRam
body:
## Description

The Paint Bucket canvas pointer is a generic crosshair. Photoshop shows a paint-bucket cursor, so the hotspot and the tool are obvious while filling.

On main, `Tool::PaintBucket` is not `is_brushlike()` (`crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`). The canvas cursor match in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` then falls through to `CursorIcon::Crosshair`. The Gradient tool takes that same fallback.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an image.
2. Select the Paint Bucket.
3. Move the pointer over the canvas.

The pointer is a paint-bucket cursor, as in Photoshop.

## Actual

The pointer is a crosshair.

Seen in PhotoCraft 0.5 on Windows in the video below. The crosshair fallback is still the path on main (checked 2026-10-12).
